title: Product Designer (m/f/x)
description:
UP42 was founded in 2019 with a clear purpose: to transform how organizations order, access, and analyze Earth observation data. Our platform brings together the world’s leading geospatial providers, and offers a single touchpoint to access, manage, and process data at scale. From vegetation management and infrastructure monitoring to disaster response, UP42 helps organizations across industries find solutions to complex problems through Earth observation. Our expert support team and detailed documentation guide our users through every step. Since July 2025, UP42 has been a part of Neo Space Group.

We are looking for a Product Designer (m/f/x) to join our Design Team in Berlin. You will be the design partner for one of our product teams, working alongside a Product Manager and engineers to take work from an early idea through to something people use. You will own your projects, hold a high quality bar on complex, data-rich interfaces, and work inside a design system you help keep healthy.
You will enjoy this role if you want real ownership of a product area without carrying a whole platform, and if you like going deep into a genuinely complex domain. Our team is complementary, so your work is visible and the feedback loop is short.

What you will do:

  • Take design work from an early idea through to delivery, proposing solutions to blockers rather than only reporting them.

  • Be the reliable design partner for your product team: the person your PM and engineers come to first.

  • Design for complexity: dense data tables, long-running processes, and workflows where the edge cases matter as much as the main path.

  • Look for evidence before you design: talk to users, read what support and sales already know, look at how the product is actually used, and run tests on your own work.

  • Push to understand the problem before designing a solution, and say so when a brief arrives already shaped as one.

  • Scope your own features, break them into pieces, be roughly right about how long they will take, and flag delays early with a plan B rather than a warning.

  • Contribute to our design system, as everyone on our team does: propose and build components, not only use them.

  • Share your work cross-functionally, take feedback, and iterate; notice improvements inside your area and act on them, instead of waiting to be asked.


Here is a good summary of what we are looking for:

  • Experience delivering product design work end-to-end inside a cross-functional team.

  • Solid interaction (IxD) and visual/UI design skills, with the ability to make complex data and workflows understandable.

  • Strong Figma skills, and a working understanding of how a design system is actually built: how a component is structured, how it behaves, and the rules it has to respect. You will be a contributor to ours, not only a user of it.

  • Experience using research and product evidence to make design decisions: usability tests, customer conversations, support tickets, product data. We are not looking for one particular method.

  • Comfortable telling the difference between what we know and what we are assuming, and willing to say which is which.

  • Comfortable with ambiguity: able to make progress when the picture is still incomplete, and to adjust when what you learn changes the direction.

  • Able to scope your own work and communicate honestly about time, collaborative, feedback-driven, and proactive about the problems you can see.

  • Fluent in English and based in Berlin with hybrid work capability.

Bonus points if you bring:

  • Experience designing geospatial, enterprise, or data-heavy B2B products.

  • Background in UX research, data visualization, or complex workflow design.

  • Knowledge of accessibility and inclusive design.

  • Experience with interactive prototyping.

  • Awareness of current AI tools and emerging opportunities in UX processes, with an understanding of how AI can enhance user outcomes without adding unnecessary complexity.

Let us tell you why UP42 is a good choice:

  • Let’s disrupt the industry: You get the chance to shape the state-of-the-art geospatial processing platform and create a completely new planetary perspective

  • Let’s stay flexible: We practice a hybrid working model - you can choose when to work from the comfort of your home or join your colleagues in our modern office in the heart of Kreuzberg, or even from a global place of your choice up to 90 days per year

  • Let’s win as a team: We’re an inspiring international team working in a fun and productive environment

  • Let’s be fair: We offer a competitive salary package and other perks such as wellbeing initiatives, sponsored fitness subscriptions, an educational budget for your personal development and public transportation discount - just to name a few

  • Let’s enjoy the good side of life: Gather in regular team events as well as our global company parties twice a year

  • Let’s think outside of the box: There are challenges and enough space for creativity and taking ownership

Does this sound like a good next step into your geospatial career? If so, we look forward to receiving your application in English.

Our culture is one of belonging, where everyone feels welcome and where differences are celebrated. We seek to recruit the best talent regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background and/or belief—and strongly encourage people from underrepresented groups to apply. We also value more than the skills and experiences outlined in this job description. Even if you think you only fill 60% of the requirements for this role - we would still like to consider your application.

title: Branch Support Manager - Europe
description:
About Rain for Rent International

Rain for Rent International provides innovative tank systems for liquid management applications. As an internationally operating rental and service company, expertise centers on rental, logistics, and services around the tank, focusing on the core competencies of renting storage tanks, containment systems, pumps, and filtration units.

Your role

We are looking for a hands-on Branch Support Manager ( m/f/d ) to help our teams across Germany, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands and France get the best from our business systems, processes and support functions.

This is not a traditional IT Manager position.

It is a highly business-facing role combining business systems, operational processes, user support, training, continuous improvement and team leadership. You will work closely with our branches and Shared Services teams to understand how people work, where they encounter challenges and how technology and better processes can make their jobs easier and our business more effective.

What you will do

Become a Business Systems Expert

You will develop strong expertise in the applications supporting our European operations and become a trusted point of contact for our business users.

A major focus will be our ERP environment, supporting processes such as:

  • Purchasing and purchase orders

  • Goods and invoice receipt

  • Rental contracts

  • Equipment on-hire and off-hire

  • Recurring and final billing

  • Credit notes and ad-hoc invoicing

  • Customer, supplier and item master data

You will also support the effective use of CRM, Microsoft 365 and other operational applications.

Experience with inspHire, Zoho or Twinfield would be advantageous, but previous knowledge of our specific applications is not essential if you have strong ERP/business systems experience and learn quickly.

Help People Get the Best From Technology

You will work directly with colleagues across our branches to understand challenges, answer questions and identify better ways of working.

That includes:

  • Providing practical systems and process support

  • Training new and existing users

  • Developing SOPs, quick-reference guides and training materials

  • Creating screen recordings and short training videos

  • Building a structured, version-controlled knowledge library

  • Identifying recurring problems and addressing their root causes

Most importantly, you will explain the why, not only the how.

Connect Systems With Business Reality

Good systems only create good information when they are used correctly.

You will therefore work closely with Operations, Sales, Finance, Fleet and other Shared Services functions to improve the quality and consistency of the processes behind our data.

You will help us ensure that operational information, CRM pipelines, rental transactions, margins and management KPIs accurately reflect what is happening in the business.

Listen, Challenge and Improve

Our branches know their business and will bring you ideas and requirements.

Your job is not simply to say yes.

You will listen, understand the underlying need and assess whether the best answer is a change to a system, process, training or something else.

For larger initiatives, you will help structure requirements, assess benefits, costs, effort and risks, and make clear recommendations to leadership.

Lead a Small Team

You will lead a developing Branch Support function, expected to include approximately three team members across business support and IT/helpdesk activities.

This remains a hands-on role. You will lead the team while actively participating in support, training, problem solving and improvement initiatives yourself.

Stay Curious

Technology is changing quickly and we want to take advantage of it.

You do not need to be an AI expert, but you should be curious about tools such as Microsoft Copilot, automation and new ways technology can help colleagues work more effectively.

The Person We Are Looking For

Systems knowledge matters, but how you work with people matters just as much.

You are someone who:

  • Listens before proposing a solution

  • Is patient and enjoys explaining things

  • Can train and support colleagues with different levels of systems experience

  • Builds credibility and strong working relationships

  • Can persuade and influence without relying on hierarchy

  • Is comfortable constructively challenging a request

  • Is pragmatic and realistic about priorities, resources and costs

  • Learns new business processes quickly

  • Enjoys solving problems

  • Is comfortable being visible and close to the operational business

  • Is curious about technology and AI

You should be equally comfortable discussing a process with a branch administrator, working through a systems problem with IT, understanding a commercial requirement from Sales or presenting a recommendation to leadership.

European Scope

The role supports operations across Germany, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands and France.

Regular interaction with the branches is a fundamental part of the position. You should therefore be willing to travel across our European locations, build strong relationships with local teams and spend time understanding how our operations work in practice.

Regular office presence is also expected, currently anticipated at up to three days per week at our office in Potsdam.

Why This Role?

This is an opportunity to shape a developing European support function rather than simply inherit an established helpdesk.

You will have the opportunity to influence:

  • How we use our business systems

  • How we support and train users

  • How processes are standardised across countries

  • How knowledge is documented and shared

  • How new technology and AI are adopted

  • How Branch Support develops as our European organisation evolves

If you enjoy bringing together people, processes and technology and want a role where you can see the practical impact of your work across the business, we would like to hear from you.

title: Senior Software Engineer (AppSec)
description:
About us

Trigger.dev is the platform for running reliable AI agents and workflows. Developers use it to build, deploy, and scale production systems with built-in tools for orchestration, scheduling, monitoring, and debugging.

Our Cloud product is a managed service where we deploy our users’ code and auto-scale from zero to millions of executions. Today, we serve thousands of teams building AI apps and agents, handling hundreds of millions of executions per month.

About the role

You’ll own security at Trigger.dev: our infrastructure, our app, the runtime that runs our users’ code, and the secrets they trust us with.

Some of our customers let their own users run code on Trigger.dev (think coding agents running whatever instructions they’re given). That code must never reach our systems or our customers’ systems. Keeping it contained is a feature we ship, so this is a product engineering role as much as a security one.

About half to three quarters of your time will be backend engineering. The rest is hunting for problems and fixing them. When you find something, you own the fix. You’ll set your own priorities and work with others when necessary.

We’re looking for an application security (AppSec) engineer who builds: a senior backend engineer who brings a security mindset to everything they ship.

What you’ll do

  • Sandbox and runtime security. Design and harden the environments that isolate untrusted user code. This is the core of the role.

  • Security features for customers. Build things like end-to-end encrypted secrets, log redaction, private networking, and runtime hardening.

  • Automated offensive testing. Use AI tools to attack our own systems on a schedule, find weak spots, and fix them. Bring in outside pen testers when it’s worth it.

  • Detection and response. Build monitoring and alerting for suspicious activity, improve our security observability, and lead the response when something needs a look.

  • Vulnerability management. Run scanning and triage, own our vulnerability disclosure program, and handle incoming reports.

  • Automated quality. Own our security PR reviews, automated scans, fixes, and triage.

  • Write it down. Document how we do security so the rest of the team can answer customer questions with confidence.

  • Security habits. Help the engineering team build secure habits with reviews, docs, and light guardrails.

Like everyone at Trigger.dev, you’ll also help in our Discord and GitHub community, write docs, and create content like blog posts, code examples, and videos.

What we’re looking for

  • Senior backend engineer. You design and ship production backend systems yourself.

  • AppSec experience. You’ve done hands-on application security work, such as secure code review, threat modelling, pen testing, CTFs or bug bounties. You don’t need a security job title or to have run a security team.

  • Cloud operations. You’ve run production systems in the cloud.

  • Multi-tenant systems. You’ve built or secured systems where many customers share the same infrastructure.

  • TypeScript. You’re comfortable working in it. Our codebase also uses Go and Rust.

  • AI-forward. You use AI tools to automate testing, detection, and defense.

  • Startup pace. You’ve worked somewhere a step or two ahead of where we are, so you know what good looks like at our size.

  • Owner’s mindset. You take work off the team’s plate and fix what you find.

  • On call. Reliability and security response are shared across the team.

  • In-person time. You’re open to team events a few times a year.

You’ll stand out if you have

  • Built or hardened sandboxes: containers, microVMs, gVisor, Firecracker, WASM, or similar.

  • Secured platforms where customers have their own customers.

  • A track record in bug bounties or CTFs.

  • Contributed to open source.

  • Worked at a developer tools, infrastructure, or open source company.

  • Experience with Go or Rust.

Benefits

  • Compensation and equity. Generous, transparent pay, plus equity so everyone shares in the company’s success.

  • Async working. Need a heads-down day or a meeting-free day? No problem.

  • Home office. We help with equipment so you’re as productive at home as in the office.

  • Vacation. 25 days plus national holidays, sick leave, and generous parental leave.

  • Training budget. An annual budget for books, courses, or an Audible subscription.

  • Pension. Join our company scheme, or we’ll pay into your private pension.

Our values

  • We’re proud to be open source. We believe in the open source community and in building a great free-to-use product.

  • We ship uncomfortably fast. Moving fast is key for a startup. We’re pragmatic about what we build and when.

  • We work autonomously. We decide as a team what will help our customers most, and prioritize from there.

title: Systems Simulation & Performance Modelling - Member of Technical Staff
description:
About Us

We’re living through a Cambrian explosion of intelligence: new models and new chips, each specialised for different tasks, are arriving all at once. The result is a new era for AI, one of radical heterogeneity.

Callosum is the Intelligent Systems Company. We believe the next generation of AI won't be defined by any single model or chip, but by intelligent systems in which hardware and intelligence co-evolve. We are building the infrastructure that unifies heterogeneous compute across the full stack. This opens a new axis of scaling intelligence: a dynamic system that tailors itself to what each workload actually needs, whether that's speed, cost, precision, or whatever unit comes next.

The last era scaled on a different bet: one bigger model, more of the same chip, more data. That bet is running into structural limits. Frontier models offer extraordinary capability at unsustainable cost, one that today's monolithic infrastructure was never designed to serve.

Our founding principle is that intelligence comes from many specialised systems working together, not from any single component. We build the software orchestration layer that co-evolves models, workflows and silicon into one system, delivering inference tailored to every workload, and demonstrating orders-of-magnitude leaps in capability and cost.

Because our software spans the full stack, our engineering team works directly with heterogeneous accelerators and frontier silicon, including Cerebras, d-Matrix, Intel, NVIDIA, AMD, Normal Computing, Tenstorrent, GreatSky, and Mixx. We are not stopping at today's chips: each new generation of silicon unlocks algorithms that couldn't run before, and we intend to be first to them, every time. If we get it right, it will belong to everyone building on it - not to any single vendor.

In our latest funding round, we raised $100M, led by Atomico with participation from Plural, DCVC and the UK Sovereign AI Fund’s first investment. With this, we are building the infrastructure for the next era of intelligence.

We are engineers and scientists based in London, working across the full depth of the stack. We are curious, intellectually honest, and building what doesn't exist yet. If you thrive on uncharted territory and are energised by the scale of the challenge, we'd love to hear from you.

About the Role

Callosum believes that scaling heterogeneous AI infrastructure requires understanding how emerging hardware will behave as part of larger computational systems. Performance characteristics measured on individual accelerators rarely translate directly to distributed deployments, where networking, memory, and execution strategies introduce new constraints. We are developing simulation infrastructure that allows us to explore these interactions and evaluate future systems before they exist.

This role advances the simulation and performance modelling tools that inform Callosum's hardware and infrastructure decisions. You will extend models that project device-level performance to rack-scale systems, explore alternative hardware configurations and execution strategies, and provide experimental environments for automated optimisation. The work also encompasses profiling, workload tracing, and performance instrumentation, connecting measurements from real systems to accurate and useful models of those we want to build.

What You'll Build

  • Extend our simulators to predict heterogeneous compute performance from individual accelerators to multi-rack deployments.

  • Model networking, memory, and execution behaviour to evaluate alternative system architectures and configurations.

  • Develop profiling, tracing, and workload capture tools that inform and validate simulation models.

  • Extend simulation environments for rapid experimentation and automated optimisation of systems and algorithms.

  • Characterise emerging accelerator architectures and translate hardware measurements into predictive models of system-level performance.

What Sets You Apart

  • Strong experience in systems simulation, performance modelling, or performance-critical systems software.

  • Deep understanding of computer architecture, distributed systems, or high-performance computing.

  • Familiarity with profiling, tracing, instrumentation, and methods for characterising computational workloads.

  • Strong systems programming experience, ideally including C++ or Rust.

  • Ability to reason about modelling accuracy, abstraction, and trade-offs between simulation fidelity and computational cost.

What We Offer

  • Competitive Salary, determined by skills and experience

  • Equity & Ownership

  • Private healthcare

  • We offer Visa sponsorship and relocation benefits to hire the best in the world

  • We work in person at our London office. You'll have the tools, space and setup to do your best work, and if you have specific needs, just tell us

title: Product Design Director - Patient (x/f/m)
description:
Product Design Director - Patient (x/f/m)

The opportunity

Doctolib is a mission-driven healthcare technology company, founded in Paris in 2013. Today, nearly 3,000 people work across Europe to transform the way healthcare is delivered and experienced.

More than 500,000 healthcare professionals use Doctolib’s solutions, and the patient app is used by approximately 90 million people across Europe.

For patients, Doctolib began as a simple way to find a healthcare professional and book an appointment. We are now building something much more ambitious: an AI-powered Health Companion that helps people navigate care, understand their health and take the right next step throughout their health journey.

This means moving beyond a primarily transactional product towards an experience that supports patients before, during and after care, through access to care, health information, patient data, messaging, recommendations, care plans and AI-powered assistance.

We are looking for a Product Design Director to help define what this next generation of patient experience should look and feel like.

What you will build and lead

As Product Design Director, Patient, you will own the design vision and quality bar for Doctolib’s patient experience. You will report to our VP Design and work closely with the Product, Engineering, Medical, Data and Business leadership teams. 

Your scope will cover the full patient journey, including:

  • access to care, search and booking;

  • patient messaging and teleconsultation;

  • the Patient Health Record and patient context;

  • the app homepage and daily health experience;

  • health content and prevention;

  • recommendations, reminders and care plans;

  • new patient services and subscription experiences;

  • conversational and AI-powered experiences.

The current team includes six Senior Product Designers and one Senior Content Designer. You will lead, coach and develop this team while shaping the organisation and operating model needed to support the next phase of the Patient product.

Your mandate

You will:

  • Define and drive the design vision for the Patient stream, from a high-traffic booking experience to a trusted Health Companion used throughout the health journey.

  • Bridge two equally important challenges: continuing to improve the core access-to-care experience while creating new reasons for patients to return beyond booking.

  • Raise the quality bar for product design, interaction design and content across the patient experience.

  • Stay close enough to the product and the craft to make high-quality design decisions, not only set direction from a distance.

  • Shape AI-native experiences that are clear, useful and trustworthy, including recommendations, conversational interfaces and next-best actions.

  • Establish strong design principles for transparency, explainability, uncertainty, user control and safe escalation in a healthcare context.

  • Build a high-performing design organisation, including hiring, coaching, talent development and second-line leadership.

  • Create effective ways of working across Design, Product, Engineering, Medical, Data and Business.

  • Help scale a coherent experience across countries, languages and different healthcare contexts.

  • Connect design decisions to user behaviour, product outcomes and business impact.

What success looks like

In your first year, you will have:

  • established a clear and compelling design vision for the Patient stream;

  • raised the quality bar across both core access-to-care journeys and newer Health Companion experiences;

  • helped define a coherent interaction model for AI-powered patient experiences;

  • strengthened collaboration between Design, Product, Engineering and Medical;

  • developed a clear operating model and growth plan for the Patient Design organisation;

  • helped Doctolib increase the value and relevance of the patient experience beyond appointment booking.

What we are looking for

You are likely to bring:

  • Significant experience leading Product Design, 10+ years in product design including 3+ years in people leadership..

  • Experience in a consumer product organisation, ideally one used by millions of people.

  • A track record of designing and scaling products across multiple markets, with an understanding of localisation, cultural differences and the balance between global consistency and local relevance.

  • Experience managing at least five Product Designers, ideally a larger organisation including senior individual contributors and managers.

  • Strong product design craft and creative judgement. You can recognise excellent work, make difficult quality trade-offs and stay close enough to the details to raise the standard of the product.

  • Experience connecting design choices to measurable outcomes such as adoption, conversion, engagement, retention, satisfaction or user behaviour.

  • A strong and practical understanding of AI-native product experiences. You have thought deeply about how AI changes interaction design, user expectations, trust, transparency and control.

  • Experience designing with uncertainty, recommendations, personalisation or conversational interfaces is highly relevant.

  • The ability to operate across complex products and stakeholders, while maintaining clarity and momentum.

  • A concise and compelling communication style. You can articulate a clear point of view, align senior stakeholders and inspire teams to move in a new direction.

  • Experience in healthcare or another regulated, trust-sensitive environment is valuable, but healthcare experience is not required. What matters is your respect for domain expertise and your ability to design responsibly in high-stakes contexts.

  • Fluency in English. French or German would be a strong plus.

  • A working style aligned with the Doctolib Playbook: User First, Medical Expertise, Forefront of Innovation, Bold, Drive, Passion, Humility.

Why Doctolib, why now?

Doctolib gives you the opportunity to work on a consumer product with significant reach, strong European scale and a mission that matters.

The patient product already has a large and engaged audience. The next challenge is to make the experience more useful, more contextual and more present in people’s everyday health journeys.

You will join at a defining moment:

  • Doctolib is moving from appointment booking towards continuous health support.

  • AI is becoming a core part of the product experience, not an isolated feature.

  • The Patient Design organisation is being strengthened and reshaped.

  • The product must work across multiple European countries, languages and healthcare systems.

  • The design foundations for the next chapter are still being built.

This is an opportunity to shape a new category at the intersection of consumer product design, healthcare and AI, and to define how people will discover, understand and manage their health in the future.

  • Contribuer à l'atmosphère et à l'expérience propres au Songe.

  • Participer à la vie quotidienne de la maison et au bon fonctionnement de l'équipe.

Le profil que nous recherchons

Au-delà de votre parcours, nous recherchons avant tout une personne investie, fiable et bienveillante, qui partage notre vision d'un bien-être authentique et profondément humain.

  • Planning : jours et horaires en semaine à définir ensemble selon vos disponibilités et les besoins de la maison.

  • Lieu : Paris 15e, métro Boucicaut.

  • Rémunération : selon profil et expérience.

  • Prise de poste : dès que possible.

Parce que nous sommes convaincues qu'une praticienne épanouie est aussi une praticienne qui prend mieux soin des autres. Nous avons à cœur de proposer un environnement de travail agréable, respectueux et équilibré.

Vous rejoindrez une maison à taille humaine qui privilégie le savoir-faire, l'écoute et la qualité plutôt que les soins standardisés. Un lieu où chaque détail compte et où l'on prend soin des personnes autant que de leur bien-être.

Nous serons ravies de découvrir votre parcours !

Au plaisir de vous rencontrer et, peut-être, de vous accueillir dans la dream team du Songe !

title: Senior Engineering Manager, Product Engineering
description:
Location: Remote (EMEA) · Germany/Munich preferred - CET/CEST time zone

Hi — I'm Grigory, co-founder and CTO at Secfix.

At Secfix we're building security compliance systems for teams and agents to become and stay compliant with less effort. We're already the category leader in Europe. AI is changing how software gets built, and we're shaping the tools this new era requires.

I've spent most of my career believing that the best engineering leaders aren't the ones who run the most meetings. They're the ones who make everyone around them faster, clearer, and more proud of their work — and they can do that because they've been through the hard technical problems themselves.

Since we started, I've done the engineering management myself: 1:1s, hiring, design reviews, performance conversations. The team is 8 engineers and 2 product designers, and I'm spread across too many things. If we were a football team, we'd be a good regional side that just made it to the Bundesliga — talented, hard-working, winning quite a few games. Now we need a coach who's played at Champions League level and can take us there to win every week.

That means a strong engineering manager who can still ship. Someone who owns the technical decisions, sets the pace, and has product taste — who notices when a feature takes three weeks that should take one, and when it ships on time but isn't good enough. You won't ship weekly — you'll need focus — but you'll build with the team often enough to know the playbook still works.

You'll work directly with me. Two things matter most here: speed and taste. Most teams pick one. We need both to win.

— Grigory


Why Secfix exists

Over 1.78 million SMBs in Europe need to comply with security frameworks — ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, SOC 2 — just to sell to enterprise customers. The process is manual, painful, and takes over a year. We automated it.

Our platform integrates with a company's full tech stack — AWS, Azure AD, Jira, GitLab, GCP, and more — automatically extracts compliance evidence, and guides teams to certification in weeks instead of months. Our fastest customer was certified in 4 weeks instead of the industry-standard 12+ months.

We've raised €17M in total (€12M Series A), backed by Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital. We're on a profitable trajectory, growing fast, and building the team that will take us to own European market from SMBs to mid market.

This space is not threatened by AI; it's amplified by it. Compliance requires deep domain expertise combined with automation. Our new AI product (CISO AI) is just getting started, and there's a huge amount of engineering work ahead: agentic workflows, intelligent evidence collection, context-aware policy generation, and more.


What you'll actually do in the first 3 months

This isn't a role where you show up and start running standups. There are no standups. Here's how the first quarter goes:

Month 1: Ship. Get into the codebase and ship a meaningful feature with AI alongside the team. You don't need to be the fastest engineer in the room, but the team needs to see that you can build at the level you'll ask of them and can ask the right questions.

Month 2: Make the team faster. Find where features take three weeks that should take one, and fix it — in tooling, in how we review and test, or in who's working on what. Start regular 1:1s with each engineer, focused on weekly output, quality, and how well they use AI.

Month 3: Own hiring. Take over engineering interviews and build a process that runs without my oversight. Design the technical challenges, run the screens, make the calls. The next people we bring in should raise the pace again. I will be there but switch my focus to final interviews.


What will the role look like beyond the first 3 months?

After the first quarter, the job is management and the technical decisions. You own how the team builds: how engineers test, how they review each other's code and security, how the team is organised, and who we hire next. We're 8 engineers and 2 product designers today and plan to be around 16 within 12 months — most of that hiring is yours to run.

You won't ship weekly, but you'll build something with the team now and then, because that's how you know the playbook still gets things out the door. Our CS and Sales leaders work the same way — they still own a small slice of the IC work, so they have skin in the game.

Here's what you'll be close to in the next months:

  • Speed. You’ll refine our software development processes to keep the team operating at high velocity. Cycle time from spec to production is your number and accountability. Tooling, review flow, how work is split, who's on what — whatever moves it.

  • Quality. Improve how engineers test and automate, how they review each other's code and security changes, and how the zero-bug policy survives a team of 20.

  • Team and hiring. Team structure, growth conversations, the hiring process, and eventually the next manager.

  • AI in the craft — and in the management. Engineers already work with an established set of encoded skills and rules — there's a whole playbook; you keep pushing that. Same for your own work: hiring, 1:1s, the recurring stuff.

What success looks like

At 6 months: The hiring process runs without me, and we've added 2 engineers through it. Sales, CS, and product all feel the difference in how fast we ship — and in quality. Our agentic engineering playbook is noticeably better because of you — you’ve added or rewritten the skills, rules, and AI review checks the team uses every day, and you lead by example in how you ship with agents.

At 12 months: The team is around 12-16, the zero-bug policy is still holding at that size, and I'm not in the engineering critical path anymore. You've found and/or coached the EM Nr. 2 to support growth.


How we work

We've written in depth about our engineering culture. Here's the short version — read the full articles linked below if you want the real picture.

  • Focus is sacred. Engineers are in fewer than 2 hours of meetings per week. We write before we meet. We use Loom for async walkthroughs, Notion for specs, Gather for pairing, and Slack only for what's urgent or lightweight. We don't do status theatre. We wrote about our thoughtful communication and our remote culture; give it a read.

    To drive it home, here's a recent calendar of an engineer who has been with us for over a year:

  • Small, temporary teams. A designer and two engineers. A backend engineer and a CS person. The group forms around the problem, ships, and dissolves. No standing squads, no permanent team structures — at least not yet. The people closest to the problem usually shape the solution.

  • AI is already part of the craft. We use Claude for product design exploration and spec drafting. Engineers work in Cursor with encoded skills and rules that live in the codebase — component patterns, folder structure, architecture choices, and the path from Figma to Angular code. AI checks code against architecture rules before human review. We have a dedicated design QA skill that compares Figma against coded output. We don't use AI to lower the bar; we use it to reach the bar faster with more iterations behind us. In case you’re interested, we wrote a piece about it here.

  • Zero-bugs. We take this seriously - this helps us to gain customer trust faster. Especially serious customer-facing problems don't sit in a backlog competing with roadmap work. Critical issues get fixed immediately. High-severity within 48 hours. Every bug has an owner. Weekly quality review as part of Monday planning. Quality as identity, in compliance, being correct isn't a nice-to-have; it's the entire value proposition. We care about edge cases, data integrity, and getting the details right. Customers notice the speed and polish before they can name it. That kind of quality builds trust. In our category, trust is the product.

  • We build what customers need, not what they ask for. Customer feedback is signal, not instructions. Best products are built by people with great taste who treat feedback as signals, not KPIs. We stay close to customers — CS check-ins, support tickets, Mixpanel events, onboarding calls — but none of these sources makes the decision for us.

This role is for you if:

  • You've managed a real team and made it ship faster. You've hired for it, run the hard conversations, and know what breaks as it grows — and you can point to where cycle time dropped because of you.

  • You know what great engineers look like. You've thought deeply about what makes them productive, what holds them back, and how to move them forward — and you can spot one in a single interview.

  • You have an exceptional IC track record before becoming a manager. You were a senior/principal engineer before you started managing — you didn't skip into management early because coding wasn't working out.

  • You have product taste. You notice when a feature ships on time but isn't good enough, and you say so.

  • You hold people to a high standard. You're comfortable giving direct feedback and having hard conversations about performance.

  • You're hands-on with AI-assisted development. You've used Cursor and Claude Code in real production work, not just toy projects. You have opinions about how AI changes the engineering workflow from ideation to release, and you want to push a team to keep getting faster.

  • You've worked in startups. You know what it feels like when there's low process, and the answer is "figure it out and ship it."

  • You think engineering culture can stay startup-like at scale. You're optimistic that a small, high-performing team can stay that way as it grows, with little process.

  • You communicate proactively in writing. In a remote team, written communication is how decisions get made and context gets shared. But you're not scared of jumping into a pair programming session either.


What we're looking for

Kraken Generation Flex
The energy industry is undergoing the largest transformation since industrialisation at an unprecedented rate of change and we are positioning ourselves to be at the heart of that change.

Our aim is to be the leading global provider of solutions that enable customers to release £30bn of value per annum from distributed energy resources (DERs). We are building a Software as a Service (SaaS) subscription business with a global addressable market of £2.4 billion per annum, by digitally connecting hundreds of thousands of DERs with energy markets.

We have already attained a market leading position and Kraken is a recognised thought leader and innovator in the industry.

🏠 Where you'll fit in:

As we enter a stage of rapid commercialisation and growth, we're looking for a Generation Flex Delivery Manager to own the successful onboarding of flexible generation and energy assets onto KrakenFlex across the EU with a focus on Germany.

This is a customer-facing delivery role with a strong technical bias. You'll manage an asset through the full onboarding journey, from initial discovery and technical analysis, through site design and gateway installation, to commissioning, testing and handover into live service.

You'll sit at the intersection of our customers, Electrical Engineering, Product and Customer Success Engineering teams. You'll need to understand both the connectivity and control architecture of our customers' assets and how those assets connect to and operate through the KrakenFlex SaaS platform.

You won't be expected to design the details of the integration solution or write the software yourself. Instead, you'll need enough technical depth across both areas to understand how they fit together, identify gaps and risks, challenge incomplete information and drive the right conversations to get a site successfully integrated.

Your role is to bring together three perspectives throughout onboarding:

Customer: What is the customer trying to achieve, and what do we need from them?

Product: How will the asset operate within KrakenFlex, and what product capabilities and configuration are required?

Engineering: How does the physical asset need to be integrated, connected and commissioned to make that solution work?

Your job is to make sure those three come together as one successfully delivered customer solution.

🚀 What you'll own:

  • Own the end-to-end onboarding and delivery of Generation Flex assets BESS (grid-scale and C&I) and RES (Wind and Solar), from initial onboarding through analysis, site design, installation, configuration, commissioning, testing and handover into live service.

  • Build a strong understanding of the Generation Flex product and SaaS platform, including how assets are represented, configured, monitored and controlled within KrakenFlex.

  • Understand how the physical site and its electrical/control systems connect into the KrakenFlex software architecture, and bring those two worlds together throughout onboarding.

  • Work closely with Product and Software Engineering teams to understand the relevant GenFlex capabilities, product modules, configuration requirements and technical constraints for each customer and asset.

  • Translate between customer requirements, electrical engineering requirements and SaaS/product requirements, making sure each group understands what is needed from the others.

  • Understand the end-to-end data and control path from the physical asset through site controls, meters, PPCs, gateways and communications infrastructure into Kraken Flex, and from Kraken Flex back to the asset where control is required.

  • Ensure that the customer's intended use of the GenFlex product is reflected in the technical onboarding solution, including the required telemetry, controls, configuration, integrations and product modules.

  • Be able to explain to customers how their site will interact with KrakenFlex, both from a physical integration perspective and from a software/product perspective.

  • Work with Product teams to identify where customer or asset requirements do not fit current product capabilities, and ensure gaps, constraints or product dependencies are surfaced early.

  • Feed recurring onboarding challenges, customer requirements and technical integration pain points back into Product and Engineering teams to help improve and scale the GenFlex proposition.

  • Be the primary delivery point of contact for customers during site onboarding, setting clear expectations around what we need from them, what Kraken is delivering and what needs to happen next.

  • Work closely with our Electrical Engineering and Customer Success Engineering teams to ensure the technical information required to integrate a site is complete, accurate and available at the right stage of delivery.

  • Review and interpret customer technical documentation including:

    • Electrical Single Line Diagrams (SLDs)

    • Network and communications diagrams

    • Site and asset specifications

    • PPC and controller documentation

    • Modbus register maps

    • IP addressing and network information

    • Functional Design Specifications

    • Metering and telemetry information

    • Hardware and connectivity requirements

  • Be confident discussing technical site architecture with customers and engineers, understanding how equipment such as generators, batteries, meters, PPCs, controllers, gateways and site networks fit together.

  • Identify missing, inconsistent or technically unclear customer information early and drive it to resolution before it becomes a delivery blocker.

  • Coordinate the preparation and review of Kraken integration documentation, including gateway architecture, communications diagrams, Kraken SLDs, integration designs and site configuration information.

  • Coordinate the Kraken Gateway delivery and installation process, ensuring prerequisites such as power, networking, connectivity and installation arrangements are understood and ready.

  • Manage readiness for key commissioning and testing activities, including:

    • Gateway installation and connectivity

    • Operational acceptance testing

    • Kraken market and service testing

  • Proactively manage delivery risks and communicate issues and mitigation plans clearly to internal and external stakeholders.

  • Surface blockers early and drive the right people together to resolve them rather than allowing issues to sit between teams.

  • Maintain clear visibility of the status and health of each site, including technical readiness, product readiness, customer actions, Kraken actions and upcoming milestones.

  • Continuously improve the Generation Flex onboarding process, identifying recurring technical, product or customer blockers and working with Engineering, Product and Operations teams to remove them.

🧠 What you'll bring to the party:

  • A strong technical background and the confidence to work closely with electrical, control systems, and networking.

  • A practical understanding of industrial networking and communications, including concepts such as IP addressing, LANs, routers, switches, VPNs and site connectivity.

  • Enough electrical engineering knowledge to understand concepts such as metering, breakers, transformers, generators, inverters, batteries and asset control systems.

  • Experience delivering technical projects involving the integration, commissioning or onboarding of physical assets, ideally within energy, renewables, utilities, industrial automation, controls or a similar environment.

  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to take a complicated technical problem and clearly explain the issue, impact, owner and next action.

  • Experience coordinating multiple teams and dependencies across customers, Electrical Engineering, hardware, installation partners and other third parties.

  • A highly organised approach to delivery, with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple sites at different stages of onboarding simultaneously.

  • The ability to proactively identify risk, remove blockers and maintain momentum in an environment where customer readiness and site timelines can change quickly.

  • A customer-centric mindset and a drive to provide an outstanding onboarding experience without compromising technical quality.

  • A pragmatic, collaborative approach and the confidence to operate in a fast-moving environment where processes and products are still evolving.

  • A strong interest in understanding how a SaaS product works end-to-end, rather than treating the software platform as a black box.

  • A drive to get things done in a collaborative, agile environment, comfortable navigating the complexity and comfortable being the regional face of site onboarding function.

  • Language: professional fluency in German and English

⭐ Bonus points

  • Experience in APIs, data flows, system integrations or cloud software architecture would be beneficial.

  • Experience in flexible generation, battery storage, renewable energy, demand response or distributed energy resources.

  • A working understanding of industrial communication protocols and controlled environments would be helpful (e.g. modbus, OPC UA

Als Operations Intern (m/w/d) spielst du eine Schlüsselrolle im Aufbau von Prozessen und Strukturen eines aufstrebenden und schnell wachsenden Technologie-Startups. Wir stellen fortlaufend für eine Praktikumsdauer von 3–6 Monaten ein.

  • Cross-functional collaboration: Collaborate with Digital Twin architects, systems engineers, and optical simulation scientists to ensure ML models meet fidelity, latency, and uncertainty requirements

  • Engineering rigor: Establish best practices for model versioning, reproducibility, testing, and documentation in a fast-moving research environment

Who You Are

Must-Haves

  • Master's or PhD in Machine Learning, Computational Physics, Applied Mathematics, Data Science, Computer Science, or a closely related field

  • Proven experience building, training, and deploying ML models for complex physical systems; strong command of deep learning (PyTorch, TensorFlow/JAX), probabilistic models, and uncertainty quantification

  • Expert-level Python; proficiency in C++ or Fortran a plus; experience with HPC environments (batch schedulers, MPI/OpenMP parallelization)

  • Fluency working with PDE-based simulation outputs, time-series sensor data, and high-dimensional parameter spaces typical of multiphysics environments

  • Hands-on experience with Gaussian processes, neural network surrogates, reduced-order models, or equivalent metamodeling techniques

  • Experience building robust ML pipelines for scientific data — including preprocessing, feature engineering, model validation, and deployment

  • Ability to communicate model behavior, confidence intervals, and limitations clearly to physicists, engineers, and non-ML specialists

  • Strong cross-functional team skills; comfort working in an interdisciplinary environment spanning physics, engineering, and software

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience with physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) or neural operators (DeepONet, FNO) applied to physical systems

  • Background in laser physics, plasma physics, high-energy-density science, or related complex physics domains

  • Experience with digital twin platforms and live integration of ML models with simulation environments (e.g., NVIDIA Omniverse, Siemens Xcelerator, ANSYS Twin Builder)

  • Familiarity with multidisciplinary design optimization (MDO) workflows, including Design of Experiments (DoE), sensitivity analysis, and uncertainty propagation

  • Experience applying reinforcement learning to physical system control or optimization

  • Familiarity with Monte Carlo methods and statistical uncertainty quantification frameworks

  • Experience with MLOps tooling (MLflow, Weights & Biases, DVC) in a scientific computing context

  • Interest in fusion energy, advanced laser systems, or high-energy-density physics

description:
🤓 About Luminovo

At Luminovo, we’re building the infrastructure that turns the electronics supply chain into something software can read and act on. Our customers use it to quote PCBAs faster, find cost savings and act on risks in their supply chain.

We serve 300+ customers, from Europe’s largest EMS to category-leading OEMs, with around 100 Luminerds across Munich, Berlin, New York and Austin. We’re backed by Chalfen Ventures, Cherry Ventures and General Catalyst. With data centers and robotics driving demand for electronics, someone needs to manage that supply chain, and they’ll need good software to do it. (Here’s why we care so much about electronics.)

🚀 Your role

Team Core is our platform team. Its job is to make all our other engineering teams more productive and to improve our codebase and infrastructure as a whole. You’ll:

  • Keep our DevOps setup and CI/CD pipelines fast and reliable

  • Build tools every team needs (e.g. interface for building permissions)

  • Act as an in-house Rust expert: our backend is a Rust monolith, and Team Core helps the other teams use good Rust patterns and architecture

  • Be responsible for the Developer Experience (DX).

  • Help our engineers use agents more productively

Other details

  • Location: remote-first, within two hours of CET. We prefer Munich > Berlin > Germany > Europe.

  • Tech stack: Rust, TypeScript + React, Postgres, Clickhouse, Redis, Kafka, Kubernetes, Helm, Flux

  • 🇺🇸 Some of the work in this role falls under US export control regulations (ITAR), so you must be a US citizen. You’ll need to be based in Europe, and if you’re currently in the US, we’ll support your relocation to Germany.

🖲️ Our tech stack

We always try to use the best tools available for the job. Don't worry, we don't need you to be familiar with all of these:

  • Main monolith is written in Rust (using actix-web as our web framework), deployed on Kubernetes

  • React and Typescript for frontend

  • PostgreSQL for persisting our data

  • Redis for caching and queues

  • Flux for GitOps

  • Honeycomb, Prometheus and Grafana for monitoring and observability

  • garden-io for developing on Kubernetes

  • Azure and Cloudflare for cloud computing

🤓 Whom you’ll be working with

  • Timon, one of our Founders

  • Alex and Tomas, two of our Staff Engineers

  • Inga, Senior Software Engineer

⚡️ Skills, knowledge, and expertise

Just so you know – we purposefully did not create a standard list of minimum qualifications for this role. ⚡️ About Luminovo

Luminovo is the first electronics supply chain platform that unites all data, processes, and stakeholders in the trillion-dollar electronics industry.

We fundamentally believe that technology is the best tool that humankind has developed to tackle the biggest challenges we face as a society today. And we want to do our share in accelerating technological progress.

We bring innovations to life faster and cheaper by creating a more connected and resilient electronics supply chain.

To date, over 300 active customers worldwide are working with us towards this shared goal. Supported by leading investors such as Cherry Ventures, General Catalyst/LaFamiglia, Chalfen Ventures, and others, we have raised more than €20 million.

Our core principles: putting people first & building great things

As a remote-first company headquartered in Munich, our brilliant team is spread across cities including Munich, New York, Austin, Calgary, Berlin, London, Valencia, Nairobi, and Verona, among others. 🌍

Our team includes a mix of product enthusiasts, people advocates, business masterminds, and engineering experts. What matters most is their drive to build great things.

We provide an authentic environment based on psychological safety to empower Luminerds from various backgrounds to succeed, grow, and focus on impact. Putting people first means that we deeply care about who our employees are, what makes them unique, and what they excel at.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Inference Performance
description:
About Tensordyne 

AI is transforming our world. It can perform cognitive functions that previously only humans could do, such as perceiving interactions across different modalities and environments - with the ability to quickly learn and then solve complex problems. Tensordyne is an AI system solution company that builds very high-performance, low-power generative AI inference systems. Our mission, through the creation of custom silicon, hardware and software, is to enable multimodal Generative AI inference acceleration at scale, with safe, sustainable, high-performance systems for our hyperscaler and neocloud data center customers. We are at the leading edge of advancing the latest research and product improvements for generative Al inference solutions that will make Al even more advantageous for compelling new generative AI applications.Tensordyne is a well funded, fast-paced startup company with headquarters in both Sunnyvale, CA, and Munich, Germany. We also have many talented team members working remotely across North America and Europe. We take care of our people and their families with comprehensive benefits, competitive compensation, flexible spending options, and recognition programs, because building category-defining technology starts with a healthy, supported team. Come join us as we shape the future of multimodal generative artificial intelligence!

The role

You'll build the software stack that takes a model from code down to the hardware: the abstractions, kernels, libraries, and tools that engineers and agents use to reach peak performance. Help optimize the latest AI models on our silicon.

Our hardware is designed to be straightforward to program, so the goal is not to hide it. The goal is to expose the right level of control at each layer, from our compiler-driven Python SDK to our low-level Rust programming stack, and to make every performance gap measurable and every fix permanent.

We're looking for a builder who understands hardware deeply and develops with agents by default. You'll own substantial parts of one of these layers and work closely with engineers across models, compilers, runtime, and hardware. Your focus is performance: where cycles, bandwidth, and communication go, and how to win them back. Number formats and model accuracy are owned by our conversion and emulation team; you'll partner with them where precision and speed meet.

What you'll do

  • Build the stack. Design APIs, kernel abstractions, and libraries in our Python SDK or Rust stack so model engineers and agents can reach high performance at the layer that fits their problem.
  • Make models fast. Take priority workloads, from LLMs to multimodal models, to peak performance on real silicon. Profile, find the bottleneck across kernels, compiler, runtime, and parallelism, and fix it at the right layer.
  • Close the gap between model and measurement. Compare measured performance against analytical models and simulation. Explain every material gap, and turn the explanation into a fix or a better model.
  • Build the agentic performance loop. Give agents the profilers, traces, counters, and benchmark harnesses to form a hypothesis, change code, and measure the result in minutes. Make the results trustworthy enough to act on.
  • Set the bar for performance. Define how we measure, track regressions, and report results.
  • Build for the next chip. Design abstractions that carry forward to future hardware generations. Work with hardware architects to test how architectural choices affect real workloads.

What we need from you

  • You understand hardware performance. You've optimized AI workloads on GPUs or custom accelerators and can reason about compute utilization, memory hierarchy, latency hiding, synchronization, and multi-chip scaling.
  • You build excellent software. You've owned substantial systems from design through production. You're strong in Python and/or at least one systems language such as Rust, C++, or C, and rigorous about interfaces, abstractions, and testing. We care about engineering quality more than a specific language.
  • You understand LLM inference end to end. You can read a new model's implementation and reason about prefill, decode, attention variants, KV caches, MoE, and parallelism, and how they map to compute, memory, and communication.
  • You build with agents. Agentic development is how you work, not an experiment. You'd rather build the loop that finds the optimization than find it by hand, and you know when the loop still needs a human.
  • You build things others succeed with. You've designed APIs, libraries, or performance tooling that other engineers adopted.
  • You drive problems to resolution. You form clear hypotheses, measure, and follow the evidence across software and hardware boundaries. You take ownership of the result.

If you hit a few of those boxes, we'd like to speak to you.

We'd be thrilled if you had

  • Experience with embedded, bare-metal, or low-level runtime programming.
  • Experience with MLIR, other compiler frameworks, or kernel DSLs such as Triton, Pallas, NKI, or CuTe.
  • Contributions to LLM serving stacks such as vLLM or SGLang, or a track record of taking end-to-end inference workloads to competitive performance on a hardware target.

Why join us

Your code will decide how fast models run on our hardware, and how easy it is for the next engineer, or the next agent, to make them faster. You'll own a layer of a new programming model, work directly with the people designing the hardware, and see your decisions tested on real silicon and carried into the next generation.

Tensordyne Values

  • Think big. Pursue ambitious technical and business goals.
  • Aim for excellence. Quality matters in everything we build and deliver.
  • Own it and get it done. Take responsibility and drive results.
  • Operate with integrity. Be direct, transparent, and respectful.
  • Win as a team. Make the people around you more effective.
  • Value different perspectives. The strongest teams challenge assumptions and bring diverse experience to difficult problems.

Tensordyne is an equal opportunity employer. We believe diverse teams are better equipped to solve complex problems and build exceptional technology. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, color, gender identity or expression, marital status, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, race, religion, pregnancy, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances.

About the role

We publish a lot of original evidence about AI search: a quarterly industry report, a public Index, and findings from our own research team. Right now each piece reaches the market on its own, and nobody owns the story that connects them.

We're hiring a Communications Lead to own that story. You'll decide the few ideas Peec should be known for, write and edit the work that carries them, and keep them consistent across research, founder comms, press, events, social and campaigns.

This is a senior individual contributor role based in Berlin. You report to the VP of Growth and work directly with our founders, our product marketer, and our research and content team.

What you'll do

  • Decide what Peec is known for. Pick the two or three ideas we want to own, the evidence behind each, and how the story develops quarter to quarter. Write it down so the rest of the company can repeat it.

  • Turn research into stories. Work with the research team to find what in the data our audience will care about most, then carry it out: the report intro, the founder post, the journalist brief, the stage premise. Same evidence, told differently for each audience.

  • Shape our social strategy. You set what Peec and our founders talk about on social and how each story runs across LinkedIn and our other channels. The social and content team runs the channels day to day. Work with product marketing so launches and the brand story say the same thing.

  • Write and edit the highest-stakes work yourself. Founder and expert pieces, press materials, campaign copy and research comms. Brief writers and producers on the rest, and hold every contributor to the same bar.

  • Run founder and expert communications. Talking points, interview prep, opinion pieces, stage remarks and founder posts on LinkedIn, with honest feedback afterwards. Make our founders and experts consistently good on the record.

  • Lead press and publisher strategy. Bring the news judgment, angles and briefing materials, and pitch journalists yourself. Treat independent coverage and sponsored placements differently.

  • Make Peec citable in AI search. We help marketing teams see and improve how AI search talks about them. Our own story should be the best-cited example in the category, and you own how ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini describe Peec.

What we're looking for

  • You've led an integrated launch at a B2B tech company, taking original research or a complex product to a clear story shipped across channels. You can walk us from raw evidence to final assets: what you wrote, what you commissioned, where the story changed and what you refused to claim.

  • You write fast, in many formats, and in someone else's voice when needed. We'll ask for recent work where your part is clear.

  • You are comfortable with data. Given a set of metrics, you can say which story holds up to a sceptical reader and which one doesn't.

title: Director of Procurement & Trading
description:
About Andercore

Andercore is the AI-native supplier of industrial materials and goods for energy and infrastructure. We execute trade and distribution end-to-end, on our own account, at the speed of compute - and we are becoming the supplier of record for the entire industry.

Industrial procurement is a €900B market in Europe alone and the largest manual market on earth. 95% of customers have no direct access to global supply chains. Materials pass through four or five intermediaries before they reach a site, and 40% of the margin evaporates on the way. For decades, the operating system of this industry was people: people to source, negotiate, finance, ship, and sell.

We built the alternative from scratch. We are the supplier. We buy from global sources and sell to European customers on our own account. Our AI runs the full trade: sourcing, quality, pricing, sales, logistics, credit, and financing. One request. A firm quote in minutes. Delivered on time. For the customer, it feels like buying from their preferred local supplier. No warehouses. No fleet. No inventory risk. Every trade is pre-sold before it is bought.

We are also the credit counterparty. Customers are scored and insured in minutes and get up to 60 days of payment terms priced into the quote itself. The working capital behind every trade is bank-funded, not equity-funded.

Where we are today:

  • Strong triple-digit-million euro turnover run rate, the majority of it from repeat customers

  • Seven European markets live, sourced from suppliers across Asia and beyond

  • 80+ people across Berlin (HQ), London, and Shanghai

  • $90M raised in equity and debt, including our $40M Series B, from Atomico, Project A, Target Global, and Inven Capital - with working capital facilities from UniCredit and KfW

The margin is in the bits. The moat is in the atoms. We are building the supplier of record for industrial materials - and redefining how global trade works in one of the largest and most essential industries on earth.

The Role

This is not a traditional procurement role. At Andercore, procurement is trading: fast-paced, market-driven, and executed daily — not on quarterly or annual cycles. You will lead a team of young and hungry category managers, through high-volume purchasing decisions in a dynamic environment where prices, availability, and supplier landscapes shift constantly.

You will own end-to-end procurement strategy and execution: sourcing, onboarding to the system, supplier negotiations and disputes, pricing, team leadership, and process design. We need someone who can think strategically and execute operationally every single day — from setting category strategy to approving individual purchase orders. You will be in the driver seat to build the first AI automated trading engine - a unique opportunity in the industrial supply space.

You report directly to the C level and sit on the commercial and operations leadership team. Andercore uses AI extensively across the business; you will be expected to leverage it to drive efficiency, margins, and scalability in procurement.

The core purpose of this role is to build one buying strategy that combines three things:

  • Spot trading, run as a repeatable system with a regular market-coverage schedule and clear KPIs;

  • Strategic buying, where you negotiate allocations, framework agreements and terms with Tier-1 manufacturers and develop private-label and direct-from-factory categories;

  • Supply planning, where you set the mix of spot, contract and stock and keep price and inventory risk under control.

Each part on its own is not enough. The job is to make them work together so that Andercore buys at the right price, secures supply when the market tightens, and never holds stock it cannot sell.

What You Will Do

  • Build and run the procurement machine: Develop and execute procurement strategies that support an 8-digit monthly procurement spend with exponential growth. Negotiate favourable terms, pricing, and contracts with suppliers on a daily basis.

  • Lead and develop the team: Manage 10+ team members, set clear priorities daily, coach emerging team leads, and create a culture of accountability and speed. You will need to be assertive and hands-on. Be the player-coach. Close deals yourself and hire the people you need to scale

  • Create scalable processes: Design, implement, and continuously improve procurement workflows, playbooks, and controls. Processes are implemented in days and weeks at Andercore — not quarters and years.

  • Own supplier relationships: Source, evaluate, and onboard suppliers. Maintain and expand a high-quality supplier network with strong retention across existing and emerging markets.

  • Drive margin improvement: Identify cost-saving opportunities, optimise purchasing decisions, and improve payment terms to boost net revenue margin and cash cycle.

  • Collaborate cross-functionally: Work closely with Sales, Customer Success, Logistics, Accounting, and Product & Engineering to align supply with demand and ensure operational excellence.

  • Full P&L responsibility: for the supply side.

  • Leverage data and AI: Use data to inform purchasing decisions, monitor supplier performance, and identify market trends. Embrace AI tools to automate and scale procurement operations.

  • AI-native procurement: automate processes from RFQs through to order confirmations, with sellers as co-designers of the agents.

What Success Looks Like

  • Revenue and margin targets consistently met or exceeded through high availability and competitive pricing.

  • A robust, high-quality supplier network with strong retention and engagement across existing and emerging markets.

  • Streamlined, repeatable processes that reduce time-to-onboard, minimise errors, and allow the team to scale without linear headcount growth.

  • A high-performing, motivated team with emerging team leads and strong cross-functional collaboration.

  • Accurate, data-driven reporting that drives continuous improvement and informs executive strategy.

  • Run a category management that unlocks and owns new product lines

Who You Are

Must-Haves

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree from a top university or business school.

  • 4+ years in a high-performance environment: for example commodity trading / high-velocity B2B procurement.

  • Proven ability to build processes and delegate effectively. You must be able to create systems that outlast your personal involvement — not do everything yourself.

  • Strong assertiveness and people leadership. You will manage a young team that needs clear direction, daily prioritisation, and coaching.

  • Ability to operate at both strategic and granular levels: setting category strategy in the morning and reviewing individual POs in the afternoon.

  • Excellent analytical and communication skills.

  • Fluent English is required; German is a strong plus.

  • Comfortable with a high-intensity, fast-paced startup environment where priorities can shift daily.

  • Proven results negotiating from the smaller side of the table, i.e. securing allocation, pricing and terms when you are not the biggest customer.
