title: UI Engineer (Based in CA or NC only)
description:
Mission: Live at the intersection of app runtime & security. Protect applications in a fundamental way so that developers can build great application services and not be constantly looking over their shoulder. BlueRock is changing the landscape of App runtime security.

The role

Location: Must be based in CA (preferably San Francisco Bay Area) or North Carolina

You will work alongside BlueRock's product designers and the control plane development team on our operator consoles. These are the React front ends that engineers and security teams use to manage large fleets of protected nodes, see what AI agents are actually doing across those fleets, and author the policy that constrains them.

The domain is AI and agentic systems, seen from the operations and security side. When an agent calls an MCP server, spawns a subagent, runs a shell command in a sandbox, or burns $40 of tokens in an afternoon, our UI is where a person sees it, understands it, and decides what to allow. So the interesting problems are visibility problems (how do you show a thousand agent sessions so someone can find the one that matters?) and control problems (how do you author an enforcement policy without a mistake taking production down?).

This is a mid-level role. We expect about 3–5 years of professional front-end experience, or equivalent work that clearly shows the same judgment. The ideal candidate is passionate about user experience, design, and AI-assisted software development, with a demonstrated grounding in engineering best practices. The title says UI, but the work doesn’t stop there: you’ll work closely with our backend services, and a feature is finished when it’s proven working live, not when the screen looks right.

Working with design delivered as code

At BlueRock, product designers design and collaborate in code. Instead of handing off static mockups, they build working UI with AI coding tools, against real data, and open merge requests. Iteration happens so quickly that it has outpaced our capacity for robust engineering collaboration and review.

This role closes that gap. You will collaborate directly with product designers and backend developers to keep UI development fast, by bridging the gap between vibe code and high-quality, sustainable, well-tested code. Some days that means reviewing and hardening a designer's branch so it can merge. Other days it means building the shared components, tests and guardrails that make the next branch need less hardening.

Beyond reviewing and hardening code, you'll help shape how it gets made. Working with designers and the AI tools they use, you'll turn what each review teaches us into shared components, conventions, tests and agent instructions. Over time the whole practice becomes more predictable, and each new branch arrives closer to production-ready.

Roles and collaboration

Software development roles are blurring more than ever. This role reports to product design, with API and data-layer guidance from our control plane engineering lead. You must be attuned to the perspectives of both UX/Design and Engineering, acting as a bridge between the goals and priorities of both sides, while ultimately deferring to UX/design partners on matters of style, copy, and information architecture.

In practice: when a designer's branch makes a choice about layout, copy or flow, you protect the intent and fix the implementation. When the implementation can't support the intent, because of performance, data shape or maintainability, you say so early and bring options rather than quietly changing the design.

What you'll do

  • Review designer-authored merge requests and bring them to production quality: structure, types, tests, accessibility, performance, and both light and dark themes.

  • Turn one-off UI from fast iteration into shared, documented components in our design system and Storybook, and migrate the apps onto them.

  • Make data-dense views hold up at real scale. Dashboards, tables, charts, and time-range and filter controls that work on a demo tenant also have to work on one with billions of events.

  • Wire UI to the API layer (GraphQL), and work with backend developers when a view needs a new query, field or endpoint.

  • Own UI test coverage: Vitest for units and Playwright for end-to-end flows, kept green in CI.

  • Test UI end to end in live, secured environments, with full authentication and authorization, real data and realistic load, before calling it done.

  • Keep UI work moving across release lines: shipping behind feature flags, and carrying fixes between branches when a release is frozen.

  • Fix UI bugs across the consoles and the Windows, Mac and Linux clients: layout and overflow, tooltips and popovers, empty and zero states, things that are technically correct and still confusing.

  • When needed, design new interfaces within the existing design system, and bring them to design for review.

  • Help set the guardrails that make AI-assisted UI development safe: lint rules, conventions, review checklists, and the instructions our AI coding tools follow.

How we expect you to work

These are the habits of a careful engineer. They matter more here, not less, because so much of the code you touch was drafted quickly by someone else or by an AI tool.

  1. Diagnose before you change. Find the actual cause, which is usually a layer away from the symptom, and be able to explain why your fix addresses it. A change that makes the symptom disappear is not the same as a fix.

  2. Small, deliberate diffs. Solve the problem in front of you. Don't refactor adjacent code on the way past, and don't build the abstraction you may need later.

  3. Fix it in one place. When the same bug shows up in three panels, the fix belongs in the shared component, not copied three times. Knowing where a change belongs is most of the skill.

  4. Verify, then claim. Run it, look at it, check both themes and a narrow viewport, get types and lint clean, and write the test where a test is what proves it. Then say plainly what you checked and what you did not. This applies double to AI-assisted work: you own the diff, whoever drafted it.

  5. Say when you're unsure. A requirement with two readings is a question, not a guess. Surfacing a problem early is always cheaper than discovering it in review.

Our UI stack and design system

Our front ends are several React and TypeScript apps that share one codebase: our enterprise operator consoles and our cloud product for builders.

All of them are built on our own design system. It is a shared React component library on top of Ant Design, with design tokens for color, type and spacing, light and dark themes, and a shared app shell for navigation, page layout and headers. Every component is documented in Storybook, published from CI, which serves as the reference for designers, engineers and AI coding tools alike. The library also carries written instructions for AI coding assistants, so generated code reaches for the system's components and tokens instead of inventing its own.

A large part of this role is the design system itself. That means promoting patterns out of individual apps into shared components, writing their stories, keeping tokens and themes consistent so the apps don't drift, and making the system the easiest path for anyone, or any agent, building UI.

  • Front end: React, TypeScript, Vite

  • Design system: our component library built on Ant Design, including design tokens and light and dark themes

  • Documentation: Storybook, published to GitLab Pages

  • Data and charts: GraphQL; ECharts for the data-dense views

  • Testing: Vitest, Playwright, and contract and smoke suites in CI

  • Delivery: GitLab merge requests and pipelines, release branches, feature flags

  • Further back: TypeScript and Rust services over graph and columnar stores, built on OpenTelemetry, plus desktop apps and services across Mac, Windows and Linux

You don't need experience with all of it. You do need to be strong in TypeScript and React, and willing to read code before changing it.

What you bring

  • About 3–5 years building production front ends in TypeScript and modern React: hooks, composition, state that lives at the right level, and an understanding of why a re-render happens.

  • An end-to-end view of the systems behind the UI. Designing in code gets a feature most of the way to working, and you close the rest of the gap. For you, “done” doesn’t stop at the UI working. It means the UI is integrated and shown to work live, in a secured environment with full authentication and authorization, under realistic load.

  • Integration testing against complex backends. Tests that only run against mock data in a standalone dev stack aren’t enough here. You can create, integrate and run tests in live environments to check data validity, load, security and scale, and you keep unit, integration and end-to-end suites green in CI.

  • Performance instincts for data-heavy UI: pagination, virtualization, server-side filtering, and knowing when a slow page is a query problem rather than a rendering problem.

  • A track record of reviewing other people’s code and improving it without rewriting it.

  • Git in complex repositories with several active release branches, where a single fix may need to be cherry-picked, ported or graft-merged onto more than one of them. Readable commits, and responding to review without taking it personally.

  • Hands-on use of AI coding tools in real work, with clear habits for checking what they produce.

  • CSS that holds up: flexbox and grid, overflow and scroll containers, responsive behaviour, and why a tooltip or popover ends up clipped.

  • Experience building or contributing to a component library or design system, ideally with Storybook and design tokens.

  • Careful attention to visual detail and real interest in UX. Much of this work is noticing that something is two pixels wrong, or that a label is technically correct and still confusing.

  • Genuine interest in the AI and agentic space, and in the operational and security questions it creates.

Nice to have: Ant Design; GraphQL; ECharts or other charting libraries; design training or a portfolio; experience on a team where designers commit code; writing conventions or instructions for AI coding tools; desktop UI across Mac, Windows and Linux; dense operational tooling such as observability, security or infrastructure products.

Not required: a computer science degree, if your work shows the same rigor. Deep backend, security or infrastructure expertise, or any knowledge of our domain (fleet management, telemetry, agent observability, policy enforcement). We will teach that.

Your first 90 days

  1. First month: land changes safely. Ship scoped fixes in the consoles. Learn the component library, theme tokens and API layer. Start reviewing designer merge requests alongside an engineer.

  2. Second month: own review on a surface. Become the primary reviewer for designer-authored UI on one product area, and extract at least one repeated pattern into a shared component.

  3. Third month: make the next branch easier. Get the flows you own covered by tests in CI, and write down the conventions and guardrails that make designer branches need less hardening.

BlueRock is a well-funded, early stage cybersecurity company founded by experienced security minded entrepreneurs. Our mission is to change the game in cybersecurity. BlueRock changes the game, enabling organizations to shift from chasing CVEs and exploits to proactively protecting the foundations of applications and computing, so that developers can build great applications without looking over their shoulders.

Founded in Ukraine and headquartered in London, UFORCE is a defence-technology company with operations across Europe, the United States and Asia.

UFORCE builds uncrewed vessels, ground robotics and aircraft, autonomy software, and the command-and-control layer that operates them together. Each platform is deployable on its own, and stronger as part of the system. Its product lines include the MAGURA family of uncrewed surface vessels, the NEMESIS family of strike platforms, the LIUT family of ground robotic platforms, and counter-UAS systems.

About the Role

We are seeking an AI Enablement Lead to equip our business development team and the wider organisation to use AI effectively in their day-to-day work. Reporting to the Director, Business Data & Intelligence, you will design and deliver practical training and coaching, monitor adoption and adherence to agreed ways of working, and provide hands-on support to colleagues who need it. You will also gather user feedback and partner with our tool builders to make our AI solutions more intuitive and valuable.

This is a hands-on individual contributor position with ownership of the enablement programme. You will begin with business development and extend coverage across the broader business, working in close partnership with leaders, functional experts, and the teams who build our tools. The role carries influence rather than line authority, and does not include management of the AI builders or ownership of technical architecture. Success means colleagues become proficient in new tasks more quickly, use approved tools consistently and correctly, and make fewer repeated errors.

What You Will Do

  • Design and deliver onboarding and continuous coaching for the business development team, covering the full business development process and the correct use of approved AI tools, reinforced through team leaders.

  • Develop role-specific playbooks and readiness programmes that help colleagues prepare effectively for customer engagements.

  • Roll out approved AI workflows to priority audiences across the company, embedding learning in the tools and systems where people already work.

  • Create task-based learning with hands-on practice, feedback, and knowledge checks, tailored to varying levels of experience.

  • Train colleagues to validate AI outputs, handle information appropriately, recognise approval boundaries, and escalate issues when needed.

  • Provide direct support to users who are struggling, diagnose whether an issue stems from user error, data, access, or the product itself, and engage the right owner to resolve it.

  • Drive sustained adoption after launch through manager reinforcement, internal champions, and workflow integration, and confirm readiness with tool owners ahead of wider rollout.

  • Monitor usage and quality to identify where tools are delivering value and where adoption is blocked, and use these insights to guide training, support, and product decisions.

  • Run a structured feedback process: capture input, triage and route issues to the appropriate owners, close the loop with users, and translate feedback into updated workflows, training, or product improvements.

  • Maintain a library of current learning materials and retire outdated guidance.

What We're Looking For

  • Proven experience in business development or revenue enablement, including designing and delivering onboarding, coaching, playbooks, or readiness programmes linked to individual and team performance.

  • A working understanding of B2B business development cycles, buyer roles, qualification, and customer preparation, sufficient to train and coach with credibility.

  • Hands-on experience using AI tools in your own work, with the ability to demonstrate an approved workflow, explain its sources and limitations, and correct course when outputs are inaccurate.

  • Strong facilitation and coaching skills, with the ability to design learning around real job tasks and communicate clearly to sceptical or time-constrained audiences.

  • A track record of driving behaviour change and adoption, including diagnosing why uptake fell short and improving it.

  • Analytical rigour: you measure proficiency, quality, and sustained use rather than attendance or login activity alone, and you follow through on feedback.

  • A collaborative, low-ego approach to working across functions, handling resistance constructively, and keeping stakeholders focused on priority outcomes.

Nice to Have

  • Business development or revenue enablement experience in B2B technology, defence, or another complex customer environment.

  • Experience in wider employee enablement, organisational learning, or change management.

  • Experience launching AI tools or programmes and measuring correct, sustained usage.

title: Organic Discovery, Growth Engineer
description:
TL;DR:
How people discover Lovable is being rebuilt in real time. They now find software through Google, AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Claude and others, and nobody has the full playbook yet. We're looking for an SEO and AEO specialist who wants to write it for Lovable and turn that visibility into subscribers and revenue. You're technical enough to land your own code and agentic enough to build the tools you need with AI. One sprint you're fixing how lovable.dev gets crawled and rendered; the next you're shipping pages for our highest-intent searches, or an agent that tracks where Lovable shows up in AI answers. Your first instinct is always: will people and answer engines find this, and does it help us grow?

Why Lovable?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.

We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.

The role

You'll own organic discoverability for Lovable. Answer engines come first, on top of a strong foundation in traditional search. You do the strategy, building and measurement, there's no queue between an insight and a live change.

You'll build most of your tools, pages and agents on Lovable itself, and take what you learn straight to the product team. Millions of apps are published on Lovable and each one needs to be found too, so what works for lovable.dev should become better defaults and guides for our users.

What we’re looking for

  • 5+ years in SEO, AEO or organic growth on a user-facing web product at scale. Results you've driven count for more than years.

  • Hands-on AEO. You've tracked how AI assistants mention and cite a brand, tested what moves it, and can show the results.

  • Deep technical SEO. Rendering, crawling, indexing, structured data, sitemaps, canonicals and internal linking at scale. When something breaks, you find out why.

  • Agentic by default. You use AI coding tools and LLM APIs to build agents, scripts and internal tools that automate audits, monitoring and reporting, without waiting on engineering.

  • You land code. You know enough web fundamentals (HTML, JavaScript, React, APIs) to work in our codebase, get changes through review into production, and own them after launch. You don't need to be a senior software engineer.

  • Strong with data. SQL, Search Console, log files, event tracking, and tests that tell you something real.

  • Good content and product judgment. You know what makes a page worth citing and cut what isn't working.

  • Motivated by the scoreboard: traffic, citations, subscribers, revenue.

What you’ll do

In one sentence: you'll own how Lovable gets found across search engines and AI assistants, and build the site, systems and tools that turn that into growth.

  • Set the organic roadmap. Decide where Lovable needs to show up across Google, AI Overviews and AI assistants, which topics and queries matter most, and what we leave alone.

  • Own the technical health of lovable.dev. Rendering, crawling, indexing, site structure, internal links, structured data and speed are yours. Keep search traffic safe through relaunches and redesigns.

  • Ship pages that win high-intent search. Use search demand, prompt data and competitor gaps to pick what to build and refresh, then ship hub pages, templates, comparisons and other page systems. Work with content and product marketing on what goes on them.

  • Get Lovable cited beyond our own site. Find the forums, communities, publications and docs that AI answers lean on for our category, and work with community, PR and partnerships to earn a place there.

  • Make experimentation cheap and fast. Build the setup that lets the team test page formats, technical changes and distribution ideas in days, keep a record of each test, and double down on what works.

  • Build the tools search runs on. Replace manual audits, monitoring and reporting with automations and agents, ideally built on Lovable, with a person checking the work where accuracy matters.

  • Own how we measure organic. Tie rankings, AI citations and organic traffic to subscribers and revenue in the warehouse, so we can invest in organic with the same confidence as paid. Say plainly where the data has gaps.

  • Help Lovable apps get found. Work with product engineering on SEO and AEO defaults (metadata, social previews, sitemaps, rendering) for the apps our users publish, and share what works as guides.

  • Share what you learn. Bring findings back to product, and share our results with users and the wider community.

  • Keep it Lovable. Search should make the site better for people, never worse.

Our tech stack

We're building with tools that both humans and AI love:

  • Frontend: React

  • Backend: Golang and Rust

  • Cloud: Cloudflare, GCP, AWS, Many LLM providers

  • DevOps & Tooling: Github Actions, Grafana, OTEL, infra-as-code (Terraform)

Please submit your application in English. It’s our company language, so you’ll be speaking lots of it if you join.

title: Product Support Engineer - EMEA
description:
Hello!

I’m Allie, Head of Support at Ashby. I’m excited to share that we’re hiring a Product Support Engineer in EMEA 🎉

We’re expanding our global Support team to provide 24/7 coverage across time zones. You’ll join a global team while establishing the technical Support Engineering presence in EMEA, with the ownership and visibility that come from being one of the first Support Engineers across European time zones. We staff across regions rather than relying on on-call rotations; we’ll discuss the specific schedule for this opening during the process.

Not sure which Support role is right for you?

We’re hiring for both Product Support Specialist and Product Support Engineer roles.

  • Support Specialist owns cases and customer communication end-to-end. Troubleshoots complex issues by navigating internal tooling — audit logs, user experience testing, and API testing — to help customers reach successful outcomes.

  • Support Engineering serves as the escalation point between Support Specialists and Product Engineering. Owns integrations, supports data mapping and data migrations for customers, and resolves escalated tickets that don't require product code changes.

Please choose the role that best reflects your experience and interests rather than applying to both. If another Support role seems like a closer match, we’ll consider that in our review.

About the role

Support Engineering is the technical layer between frontline Support and Engineering. You’ll take on complex issues involving integrations, APIs, permissions, data, reporting, migrations, and workflows—using application behavior, logs, databases, and customer context to determine whether an issue can be resolved through Support or represents a product defect.

You’ll investigate issues end to end using tools such as Plain, GitHub, Datadog, databases, and the codebase. You won’t write the fix; you’ll give Engineering a well-validated escalation with reproduction steps, relevant evidence, customer impact, and a root-cause hypothesis when possible. You’ll also identify recurring issues, improve documentation and enablement, and partner with Product and Engineering on improvements. As an early Support Engineer in EMEA, you’ll establish regional operating practices and handoff norms across European time zones while bringing EMEA customer patterns to a global team.

What you’ll own

  • Own complex technical issues from intake through resolution or escalation—investigating APIs, integrations, logs, data, configuration, and workflows to determine whether Support can resolve them or Engineering should be involved.

  • Set a high bar for complex technical investigations and ensure Engineering receives clear, actionable, well-validated product issues.

  • Build trusted working relationships with frontline Support, Engineering, Product, Customer Success, and customers.

  • Identify recurring problems and turn them into documentation, enablement, tooling, process improvements, or product feedback.

  • Partner with Product and Engineering on recurring product improvements by synthesizing customer patterns, validating defects, and sharing the technical context needed to choose between a product change, documentation, tooling, or process improvement.

  • Establish EMEA coverage, handoff, and operating practices across European time zones while bringing regional customer patterns to the global Support Engineering team.

  • Track and improve the outcomes that matter: resolution speed, escalation quality, fewer avoidable Engineering escalations, frontline self-sufficiency, reduced customer effort, and customer confidence.

You should apply if:

  • You’ve worked in a hands-on, customer-centric technical role where you independently investigate ambiguous issues involving APIs, integrations, logs, data, and application behavior.

  • You’re comfortable moving between customer conversations, APIs, logs, databases, product behavior, and code-level context to find root causes.

  • You can distinguish a configuration, data, documentation, or enablement issue from a true product defect—and explain your reasoning clearly.

  • You write precise investigations that others can quickly understand and act on, and communicate thoughtfully with technical and non-technical audiences across time zones.

  • You naturally look beyond the immediate ticket and improve the systems around it through documentation, enablement, tooling, or process design.

  • You want to be an early technical owner for EMEA and are energized by building regional structure within a global team.

You should not apply if:

  • You’re looking primarily for a high-volume support role centered on predefined troubleshooting steps, rather than open-ended technical investigation and ownership.

  • Most of your experience is in internal IT, help desk, endpoint, hardware, network, infrastructure, cloud operations, systems administration, infrastructure maintenance, or service deployment—and you haven’t worked extensively with customer-centric SaaS applications, APIs, logs, or data-backed troubleshooting.

  • You prefer to pass difficult issues to another team rather than reproduce, investigate, and explain them yourself.

  • You’re looking for a role focused mainly on writing production code; this role diagnoses and escalates bugs but does not own code changes.

  • You prefer clear-cut problems and predefined answers over working through ambiguity with careful documentation, focused questions, and evidence-based decisions.

  • You want a narrowly defined role without regional operating ownership or projects that improve how the broader Support team works.

Ashby builds a suite of products that helps talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run their hiring process significantly better. We raised a $50M Series D in July 2025 and support nearly 5,000 customers, including Shopify, Snowflake, OpenAI, Deliveroo, and Confluent. We’re growing much faster than 100% year over year, with a team of roughly 300 people across 22+ countries. Learn more at ashbyhq.com.

About Go To Market

We view our Support team as an extension of the product itself, one that ensures an optimal customer experience for customers ranging across all market segments. Here are a few points that should give you an idea of what it is like to work with us:

  • We spend a lot of time building best-in-class products since we believe a highly differentiated product is easier to sell.

  • We also spend a lot of time building a best-in-class customer experience. We aim to offer deep expertise whenever we interact with prospects and customers.

  • We strongly believe that small teams with very talented people and the right work environment deliver much better performance than teams with large headcount.

You can take a look at our Leadership Principles to get a sense of what we value in People Leaders at Ashby.

You’ll learn the product and support workflow, get familiar with the tools and systems used for technical investigations, and build relationships across Support, Product, and Engineering. With support from your manager and onboarding buddy, you’ll take on increasingly complex investigations as you build context, with regular check-ins throughout your first 90 days.

description:
About BJAK

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

 

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

 

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

 

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

 

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

 

The Role

BJAK is building a Neobank Superapp for Southeast Asia. As a Technical Product Manager, you’ll own a product vertical end to end—such as payments and expense management, remittance, insurance, or wealth and trading—from strategy, outcomes, and roadmap through to the technical design and delivery of the systems behind it.

 

This is a product where real money moves, mistakes are immediately visible, and licensing, compliance, and third-party rails are core product constraints—not considerations around the edges.

 

We are AI-native by default, but AI is a means, not the goal. The bar is knowing where a model can genuinely improve an outcome, where deterministic systems must remain in control, and how to build products that are reliable, auditable, and trusted when money is involved.

 

What you'll be doing

  • Own a vertical end-to-end — outcomes and metrics, a backlog prioritised by value / risk / dependency / strategic priority, acceptance criteria crisp enough to build and test against.

  • Shape the technical design with engineering — system boundaries, money-movement correctness (idempotency, ledgering, reconciliation), third-party-rail reliance and rail-down behaviour, failure/retry/refund paths, security, latency, scalability, recovery.

  • Make hard trade-offs across correctness, speed, cost, reliability and UX — and defend them to an engineering, compliance or ops lead who pushes back.

  • Treat regulated constraints as first-class product inputs — licensing scope, CDD/KYC and limits, sanctions/PEP screening, transaction monitoring, data residency and privacy. Know which are hard launch gates and which are forward-readiness.

  • Apply AI where it earns its place — define what it's allowed to decide, where a human stays in the loop, how it's evaluated, and what it does when unsure. Every AI-surfaced number traces back to a real record.

  • Ship against external gates — build feature-complete behind flags; go live per rail as each partner and regulatory gate clears.

  • Work across Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance/Reconciliation.

     

What you'll need

  • Product leadership — significant experience owning a complex technical product end-to-end; strong judgement and decisiveness under ambiguity; ability to balance ambition against technical, regulatory and operational reality; can hold their own with senior engineers.

  • Technical foundation — solid system design (boundaries, datastores, queues/workflows, APIs, failure modes, consistency under concurrency); comfort reading, reviewing and challenging design docs; can sketch an architecture and a sequence. No production code, but technical enough that engineers don't have to simplify.

  • Domain — experience in a regulated / high-consequence domain (payments, banking, remittance, insurance, …) or demonstrable fast-ramp ability; understands why money movement is different (correctness over convenience, irreversible states, partners you don't control).

  • AI judgement — hands-on with LLM-based products; can frame a feature as eval-able (offline, online, human feedback); realistic on hallucination/drift/data gaps, including data-blocked vs model-blocked and when a model must not be in the loop at all.

  • Nice to have — engineer or highly-technical-PM background · zero-to-one · shipped AI-heavy consumer products · defined eval metrics for ML/LLM systems · AI UX + failure-handling intuition · SEA market experience.

     

Outcomes

  • Clear vertical strategy and legible roadmap

  • Ships fast and clears the gates that actually block launch

  • Money is correct and users are never misled about the state of their funds

  • AI features are valuable, predictable and trusted

  • Trade-offs made deliberately under uncertainty and hold up when challenged

  • Engineering, design, compliance, and operations are aligned with minimal friction

     

Location

This role is based in UK. This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our London office at least 3 days per week.

 

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

 
 

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

1. Online assessment or practical task

2. Role-specific interview

3. CEO / final round

 

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

description:
termios macht Heizen in Wohn- und Gewerbeimmobilien smarter und klimafreundlicher. Unser Thermostat spart spürbar Energie und hilft Asset Managern, Wohnungsunternehmen und Eigentümern, ihre ESG- und Net-Zero-Ziele zu erreichen.

termios ist ein 2023 gegründetes Joint-Venture von mantro als Company Builder, dem sauerländischen Familienunternehmen Oventrop und der Düsseldorfer LEG Immobilien SE. Als Technologieunternehmen entwickeln wir grüne Lösungen rund um Heizen, Nachhaltigkeit und ESG für Wohnimmobilien.

Warum wir diese Stelle besetzen

Unser Thermostat termios Pro übernimmt den hydraulischen Abgleich automatisch, für jeden einzelnen Heizkörper, und ist in tausenden Wohnungen verbaut. Daraus entsteht ein Messdatenbestand zum realen Heizbetrieb im Gebäudebestand, wie ihn kaum ein einzelnes Forschungsprojekt aufbauen kann.

Wie viel Energie spart der automatische Abgleich wirklich, unter welchen Bedingungen, und wie weist man das sauber nach? Diese und ähnliche Fragestellungen wollen wir gemeinsam mit Hochschulen, Forschungsinstituten, Wohnungsunternehmen und Fördergebern beantworten.

Du startest dabei nicht bei null: Wir haben bereits zwei vom BMWE geförderte Forschungsprojekte und sind in weiteren Forschungsfeldern aktiv. Für dieses wachsende Portfolio suchen wir zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt jemanden, der Forschung nicht nur organisiert, sondern selbst betreibt.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Studiendesign und Feldversuche: Du übersetzt offene Fragen in prüfbare Hypothesen und ein belastbares Studiendesign mit Vergleichsgruppen, Baseline, Witterungsbereinigung und Messkonzept. Messkampagnen in realen Liegenschaften setzt du gemeinsam mit Field Service und Anlagentechnik um.

  • Datenanalyse: Du wertest Zeitreihen aus dem Gerätebestand und aus Messkampagnen selbst aus, quantifizierst Effekte und Unsicherheiten und trennst sauber zwischen Korrelation und Wirkung.

  • Ergebnisse: Du bereitest Erkenntnisse für Abschlussberichte, Fachpublikationen, Konferenzen und Kunden auf und sorgst dafür, dass sie in unsere Algorithmen und Produktentwicklung zurückfließen.

  • Projektleitung: Du steuerst mehrere parallel laufende Forschungs- und Pilotprojekte, von Arbeitspaketen und Meilensteinen über Budgets und Berichtspflichten bis zu Kooperationsverträgen, Datenschutz und Förderrichtlinien.

  • Förderung und Akquise: Du findest passende Förderprogramme auf Landes-, Bundes- und EU-Ebene, entwickelst Projektideen mit Partnern und schreibst Skizzen und Anträge.

Das bringst du mit

  • Studium: Du hast ein abgeschlossenes Studium in einem ingenieur-, natur- oder datenwissenschaftlichen Fach, z. B. Gebäude- und Energietechnik, Versorgungstechnik, Bauphysik, Physik, Mathematik oder Informatik.

  • Forschungserfahrung: Du hast mehrere Jahre in der angewandten Forschung gearbeitet, etwa an einem Fraunhofer-Institut, einer anderen Forschungseinrichtung, einer Hochschule oder in einer F&E-Abteilung, idealerweise im Umfeld Gebäude, Energie oder TGA.

  • Methodik und Daten: Du hast Studien oder Messkampagnen selbst konzipiert und ausgewertet, wendest statistische Verfahren wie Regression, Zeitreihenanalyse und Hypothesentests sicher an und arbeitest dabei mit Python oder R sowie SQL.

  • Projektleitung: Du hast Projekte mit mehreren Partnern geleitet oder koordiniert und bringst unterschiedliche Interessen zusammen.

  • Kommunikation: Du schreibst klar und belastbar, vom Förderantrag bis zur Veröffentlichung. Du sprichst verhandlungssicher Deutsch und Englisch auf Arbeitsniveau.

Das ist ein Plus

Niemand bringt alles mit. Vieles davon lernst du bei uns.

  • Förderprojekte: Du hast schon Anträge geschrieben oder öffentlich geförderte Projekte abgewickelt.

  • Heizungstechnik: Du kennst dich mit Heizungshydraulik, hydraulischem Abgleich und Wärmeerzeugern wie Fernwärme oder Wärmepumpe aus.

  • Einsparnachweise: Du kennst Verfahren zur Messung und Verifikation von Einsparungen, z. B. IPMVP.

  • Modelle: Du hast Erfahrung mit Gebäudesimulation (z. B. Modelica, TRNSYS) oder Machine Learning.

  • Promotion oder eigene Publikationen

Gute Gründe, um bei uns durchzustarten

  • Forschung, die ankommt: Wenn du eine Hypothese an einem realen Gebäude prüfen willst, organisieren wir das. Was du herausfindest, landet im Produkt, und Veröffentlichungen sind ausdrücklich erwünscht.

  • Alles unter einem Dach: Hardware, Firmware, Funk, Cloud und Daten. Wer das gebaut hat, wonach du fragst, sitzt im selben Team.

  • Gestaltungsfreiraum ab dem ersten Tag, in einem agilen Team mit flachen Hierarchien und kurzen Entscheidungswegen.

  • Flexibilität: Du arbeitest hybrid in Düsseldorf oder München, mit flexiblen Arbeitszeiten.

  • Konditionen: Unbefristete Festanstellung, wettbewerbsfähige Vergütung, 30 Tage Urlaub, Urban Sports und Corporate Benefits sowie regelmäßige Teamevents.

Klingt nach dir?

Dann freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung mit Lebenslauf, gern mit Publikationsliste oder Links zu deinen Projekten. Ein Anschreiben brauchen wir nicht. Schreib uns lieber ein paar Sätze dazu, welche Forschungsfrage dich bei uns besonders reizt.

title: Senior Privacy Counsel (m/f/d)
description:
Deep Blue Recruitment is working with an international technology company looking to appoint an experienced Senior Privacy Counsel to join its legal team.

Operating in the enterprise technology sector, the business develops software and digital solutions for customers across a range of industries. With continued investment in emerging technologies, including AI, data protection is becoming an increasingly important consideration in how the business develops its products, manages risk and works with customers.

We're looking for a commercially minded privacy lawyer who enjoys working closely with the business, understanding how technology works and finding practical solutions to complex legal questions.

This is a broad, hands-on role combining privacy advisory work, commercial support and the continued development of internal data protection processes.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Advise colleagues across the business on a broad range of privacy and data protection matters, providing clear, commercially focused legal guidance.

  • Work closely with product, technology and commercial teams on the development of new services, ensuring privacy considerations are addressed early in the process.

  • Support the negotiation of commercial agreements, particularly around data processing, international transfers, customer relationships and third-party arrangements.

  • Advise on GDPR and other applicable international data protection regulations, helping the business understand and manage its obligations across different markets.

  • Provide legal guidance on emerging technologies, including AI, and the implications of new products and data processing activities from a privacy perspective.

  • Review and improve existing privacy policies, internal procedures and governance frameworks to ensure they remain practical and fit for purpose.

  • Work alongside information security and IT teams on data governance, risk assessments and privacy-related incidents.

  • Identify opportunities to improve the efficiency of privacy operations, including through automation and better internal processes.

  • Monitor regulatory developments affecting technology businesses, particularly around data protection, AI and digital services.

  • Provide training and guidance to colleagues across the organisation, helping non-legal teams understand their responsibilities when handling personal data.

What They're Looking For

  • A German-qualified lawyer (Volljurist:in), having successfully completed both State Examinations.

  • 4–10 years of experience specialising in data protection, privacy or technology law, and significant experience advising B2B technology businesses, either in-house or in private practice.

  • Strong knowledge of GDPR and European data protection law, with proven experience applying these regulations in B2B software, SaaS, AI or technology infrastructure environments.

  • Hands-on experience advising companies that develop or provide enterprise software, AI platforms, cloud infrastructure, APIs or other data-intensive B2B technology solutions.

  • A good understanding of AI technologies, particularly AI models, infrastructure and enterprise applications, and the privacy and regulatory challenges associated with their development, deployment and commercialisation.

  • Experience negotiating and advising on B2B commercial agreements, including data processing agreements (DPAs), international data transfers, enterprise customer contracts and complex controller/processor arrangements.

  • Comfortable working closely with product, engineering and infrastructure teams, understanding technical architectures, data flows and product development processes to provide practical, commercially focused legal advice.

  • A commercial approach to risk management, with an understanding of the challenges facing high-growth B2B technology companies and the ability to find workable solutions that support product development and commercial objectives.

  • Experience working within an international B2B technology business, particularly one scaling its enterprise customer base or operating across multiple jurisdictions, would be beneficial.

Why Consider This Opportunity?

This is an opportunity to join an international technology business where privacy plays an important role in how the company operates, develops its products and works with customers.

You'll have a broad remit, working closely with different teams across the organisation on a range of commercial, operational and regulatory matters, including some of the challenges emerging technologies bring to data protection.

If you're a privacy lawyer who enjoys working closely with the business, has an interest in technology and takes a practical approach to solving legal challenges, we'd be interested in hearing from you.

The next frontier is physical: robots taking over more and more of the work in our fulfilment centres, until fresh food moves from producers to households at a cost nobody else can match.

We are setting out to record how our own people handle groceries and to turn those recordings into a training corpus for manipulation policies.   • The capture spec. Cameras, mounts, calibration, and what disqualifies an episode. You write it before we buy the fleet and enforce it after. When the spec and the floor disagree, you go to the floor and find out which one is wrong.

  • Ground truth. Hand pose is the signal that transfers from human video to robot policies, and warehouse reality — work gloves, occlusion, cold halls — is exactly where the published models struggle. You own how we measure that and how we close the gap.

  • The evaluation harness. The corpus only counts if a policy can train on it. You build the harness that decides which hours make the bank, and you hold the trainability bar as the volume grows.

  • The first training runs. Once hours bank, you post-train open robot-learning models on our data and run the first task evaluations.

  • Judgment before spend. The field moves monthly. You read what is published, reproduce the claims we depend on, and steer our capture before the money is spent, not after.

The scope

This is a seat on a small, newly created team: an operations lead who runs capture on the floor, a data engineer who owns the pipeline, and you: the machine-learning voice in the room. This is not a research-scientist role, and no publication record is required. The job is to make a corpus trainable and to train the first policies on it.

What we are looking for

  • 3+ years of relevant full-time robotics experience.

  • PyTorch, and computer vision with real 3D geometry. Camera calibration, pose estimation, SLAM fundamentals. You have debugged an extrinsic calibration at least once in your life and know why it drifted.

  • You can read a paper and reproduce it. Our pipeline is assembled from published work, and your job is knowing which claims survive contact with a chilled warehouse hall.

  • You know what policies train on. Familiar with the current robot-learning stack and policy classes well enough to know what the training side will demand of the data before the data exists.

What success looks like in 90 days

You have written the capture spec and we set up the first rigs against it. Your pilot gates have numbers, the first hours have passed your harness, and you can tell the people who sign the budget, with data, what the next hundred hours should look like.

Take this role if you would rather own the spec that decides whether a dataset becomes an asset or a write-off than tune someone else's model on someone else's data, if a fulfilment centre at 6 a.m. sounds like a lab to you, and if you want the shortest possible line between your technical judgment and a capital decision. title: Cyber Exposure Management Expert (m/w/d)
description:
It all starts with the mission: NVISO is here to protect European society from potentially devastating cyber attacks. This means we offer cyber security services to private and governmental organizations to help them better prepare for, prevent, detect and respond to cyber security incidents. All of this is built on four fundamental values that define who we are: We are Proud, We Break Barriers, We Care and No BS!

Tasks

As Cyber Exposure Management Expert (m/w/d) located in Germany, you will be the technical lead for developing NVISO's Cyber Exposure offering. You will define how Vulnerability Management, Asset Management, hardening, Patch Management, reporting and remediation work together through clear processes and responsibilities, and guide the technical decisions that make the service work for our clients.

You will be the expert clients and colleagues turn to for the complete picture: which assets matter, where they are exposed, who needs to act and whether remediation has worked. You will design the processes, integrations and reporting that connect these questions, lead complex customer engagements and help other consultants deliver the service. You will advise on hardening and help clients establish ownership, remediation targets and a process that fits their IT operations.

You will also shape what we build next. Starting from our existing Vulnerability Management capabilities, you will develop the technical roadmap towards Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM) and assess where Attack Surface analysis, exposure validation and Quantum Readiness belong in the offering. This gives you room to propose solutions, build prototypes and test them with clients before turning them into repeatable services.

Typical responsibilities include:

  • Defining the technical architecture and delivery approach for the Cyber Exposure offering, connecting Vulnerability Management, Asset Management, hardening, Patch Management, reporting and remediation, with clear roles and governance;
  • Leading technical delivery on customer engagements, advising on remediation and hardening, resolving design and integration problems and reviewing the quality of our work;
  • Linking vulnerability findings to asset inventories, CMDBs, cloud environments, business services and owners, and resolving gaps in coverage and data quality;
  • Designing remediation processes with owners, priorities, SLAs, escalation, risk acceptance and closure checks, aligned with Change Management and supported by ITSM, Patch Management and other remediation solutions;
  • Building reporting that shows clients their exposure and remediation progress, with clear priorities for technical teams and reliable measures of coverage, ageing, SLA performance and accepted risk for management;
  • Advising on secure configurations and hardening baselines for infrastructure and cloud environments, reducing unnecessary exposure and proposing compensating controls when patching is not immediately possible;
  • Keeping up with developments in Exposure Management and evaluating AI and agentic solutions through targeted pilots to improve existing approaches to prioritization, remediation guidance and reporting. You will test accuracy and usefulness, protect client data and define human oversight, including approval before AI recommendations trigger remediation actions;
  • Turning client needs into service packages, technical standards and delivery methods, coaching consultants and providing technical input for proposals and scoping;
  • Developing the service roadmap and evaluating new capabilities through pilots, including CTEM, Attack Surface analysis and cryptographic discovery, Crypto Agility and Post Quantum Cryptography migration planning. You will help decide which capabilities are ready to become services and what we need to deliver them well.

Requirements

  • You hold citizenship in one of the 32 NATO member states or the Austrian citizenship;
  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in a relevant field, or equivalent professional experience;
  • Strong practical experience in Vulnerability Management, including scanning platforms, prioritization based on asset criticality and exploitability, and remediation processes, with the ability to guide technical decisions on customer engagements;
  • Understanding of enterprise infrastructure, networking and cloud environments, with practical experience advising on secure configurations, hardening baselines and compensating controls;
  • Experience connecting security findings with asset inventories, CMDBs or Asset Management platforms, including ownership mapping and improving data quality;
  • Experience designing security dashboards and management reports that make priorities, progress and data limitations clear;
  • Experience designing remediation processes across security and IT teams, including ownership, SLAs, exceptions and Change Management. Familiarity with ITSM and remediation platforms is expected; scripting and API skills are an advantage;
  • Ability to design a solution across several tools and processes, explain the technical choices and guide colleagues through implementation. Experience developing a consulting service is an advantage;
  • Interest in developing CTEM and Quantum Readiness services and testing AI applications in security operations. Experience evaluating AI or agentic solutions is an advantage. Experience with Attack Surface analysis, Crypto Agility or Post Quantum Cryptography is welcome; you do not need to be an expert in every area on day one;
  • Fluent business English and professional fluency in the relevant local language(s).

Benefits

We have multiple SANS Instructors working at NVISO, our staff has presented at popular hacking conferences (BlackHat, BruCON, OWASP, etc) and all of our technical staff can acquire deep technical security certifications (GSE, GXPN, GREM, GCFA, OSCP, etc);

Making that feel simple is a design problem and an engineering problem at the same time, and this role sits right on that seam.

 

🌲 About Spruce

  • Almost 20% of the UK's carbon emissions comes from heating homes – there's simply no way to reach net zero without phasing out gas and oil boilers. Right now the only serious alternative is heat pumps, with their almost-magical ability to turn 1 kW of electricity into 3-5 kW of heat (🤯). But the heat pump installation journey is slow, inefficient, and just so painful. This makes it hard for existing installers to grow their businesses and puts off gas engineers from starting to do heat pumps. Perhaps most critically, it means you can't currently offer a heat pump when someone's boiler breaks and they urgently need heating.

  • We're fixing this. We've built a platform for heat pump installers to manage the whole installation journey from initial enquiry through to final compliance paperwork, freeing up their time to focus on what really matters: doing high-quality installations, providing great customer service, and scaling their business. Despite only getting started at the beginning of 2024, we're having a massive impact on installation businesses, suppliers, and manufacturers across the UK: halving the time they spend on each job and doubling their sales conversion rates.

  • We raised a chunky Seed round last year from top-tier investors and this year have grown the team 3x and revenue 4x. We've expanded into Ireland, are launching an end-to-end solar and battery product in November, and are increasingly becoming the operating system for the whole home renewables supply chain. If you can picture a combination of ServiceTitan, Procore, and AutoCAD, you might get a sense of where we're headed…

 

🥖 The role

You'll own how the product looks, feels and behaves wherever installers use it, from the first sketch to the shipped feature. Installers only adopt Spruce if it's easy to use on a real job, and adoption is what drives our growth. That puts your work at the centre of the business. Day-to-day you'll be:

  • Designing and shipping – You'll take a flow from rough idea all the way to production, prototyping in whatever gets you to an answer fastest (often code, sometimes Figma or a sketch), and testing with installers as you go. The gap between "we should fix this" and "it's fixed" is often a day.

  • Owning the interaction layer – You'll build and look after the component library and the patterns underneath it: motion, loading and empty states, touch targets that still work with gloves on. The small things that make a complex tool feel simple.

  • Building the parts that are hard to get right – The canvas-based floor plan and system design tools, the offline survey app (incl. LiDAR), the proposals homeowners see. These are the parts where the UI is the product, and where we've got the most still to build.

  • Raising the bar on everything we ship – You'll work closely with our product designers and developers, pairing on their work and reviewing it, so the quality of what you build rubs off on the rest of the product.

  • Spending time with installers – You'll go out on site, watch how the product actually gets used, then come back and change it.

You'll report to Steph, our co-founder and CPO (she’s pretty awesome) and you’ll work alongside Dan & Arron who’ve cooked up some incredible work in their time so far.

 

🫵 About you

We look for the same five things in everyone at Spruce: curiosity; intense drive, ambition and work ethic; a high degree of personal agency and ownership; deep humility and a growth mindset; and excellent craft.   • Systems thinking – You enjoy the structure of a good component library and understand that consistency is what lets a small team ship fast. You also know when to slow down first: you value time spent on lo-fi wireframes and on understanding the data model before anything gets polished.

  • Curiosity about the domain – You want to understand how heating systems, solar and battery actually work, and you pick up technical detail fast. By the end of week two you'll be arguing about the best way to show a homeowner their solar self-consumption.

description:
About TACTILIA

At TACTILIA, we are building the industry-ready robotic hand that closes one of the biggest gaps in Physical AI. Spun out of Schunk, the global market leader in gripping technology, we combine a decade of robotic-hand expertise and real industrial access with the speed and ambition of a deep-tech startup.

This isn't a research project waiting for its first customer. We already have a product, customers are ready to use it, and we are launching now. Your work will directly shape the electronics, actuators, and embedded systems that make that possible.

You will join at the moment when the hard engineering questions become real product decisions: how do we make a highly capable robotic hand reliable, manufacturable, serviceable, and simple enough to deploy on a real shop floor?

The Role

As a Senior Sensor Engineer (Tactile & Proprioception) at TACTILIA Robotics, you will build the neural architecture of physical touch and spatial awareness that gives our robotic hands human-like dexterity.

You will own the complete sensing architecture—from evaluating tactile technologies and proprioceptive layouts to designing readout electronics, calibration matrix algorithms, and real-time sensor pipelines.

Fitting high-density sensing skins, force feedback, and position tracking into a tight hand envelope means balancing signal integrity, low latency, and mechanical durability under high cyclic wear. You will work closely with Mechanics, Electronics, and Software to turn raw physical contact into clean, reliable data for real-time robotic control.

What you will do:

  • Own the sensing architecture. Lead the evaluation, selection, and overall design of tactile and proprioceptive sensing systems across fingers, palm, and joints—built for modularity across product variants, not a one-off prototype.

  • Develop tactile array hardware. Design and prototype high-resolution tactile sensors (optical, capacitive, piezoresistive, or magnetic) tailored for space-constrained, contact-rich finger pads and palm surfaces.

  • Engineer proprioceptive feedback. Implement joint- and drive-level feedback mechanisms, including high-precision position/angle sensing, strain gauge force bridges, load cells, and tendinous tension tracking.

  • Design readout electronics & AFEs. Build low-noise analog front-ends (AFEs), signal conditioning circuits, and local readout hardware optimized for minimal latency, wide dynamic range, and high immunity to electromagnetic interference (EMI).

  • Build calibration & processing pipelines. Implement automated calibration protocols, thermal/drift compensation matrix algorithms, and feature extraction (e.g., slip detection, contact point estimation) to feed clean telemetry to the software stack.

  • Characterize & validate on real hardware. Own sensor testing on custom rigs—evaluating dynamic response, force linearity, hysteresis, spatial resolution, and long-term mechanical wear over hundreds of thousands of cycles.

  • Drive sensor manufacturing & yield. Partner with specialized suppliers on Design for Manufacturing (DFM) for flexible/rigid-flex PCBs, molded tactile skins, and elastomeric components, ensuring high assembly yield and second-sourcing.

  • Work across the whole team. Tight loop with Mechanics (for load paths and physical packaging), Electronics (for board interfaces), and Software (for state estimation and closed-loop grasp control).

What you bring:

  • Degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Physics, Sensorics, Robotics, or a related field.

  • 5–10 years of experience developing sensor hardware, mechatronic instrumentation, or sensor fusion systems, including at least one product taken into series production.

  • Deep domain expertise in tactile sensing modalities (e.g., optical tactile/GelSight style, piezoresistive, capacitive) or high-density proprioceptive feedback (encoders, strain gauges, load cells).

  • Proven experience in analog circuit design, signal conditioning (AFE), active filtering, and high-SNR data acquisition for physical sensors.

  • Hands-on experience with sensor calibration techniques, thermal/hysteresis modeling, signal processing, and standard communication buses (SPI, I2C, CAN).

  • Practical experience designing or integrating flexible PCBs, molded elastomers, or miniaturized mechatronic assemblies into tight physical envelopes.

  • A strong hardware mindset: you enjoy lab bring-up, sensor characterization on test rigs, and tracing physics-to-signal anomalies with scopes and logic analyzers.

  • Fluent in English; German is a plus, not a requirement.

Bonus:

  • Background in real-time embedded C/C++ firmware or ROS/ROS2 for sensor data processing and filtering.

  • Experience with tactile algorithms for slip prediction, texture recognition, or contact shape estimation.

  • Experience with soft robotics, stretchable electronics, or conductive polymers.

  • Knowledge of Machinery Regulation, ISO/TS 15066, and sensor design for collaborative applications.

The next chapter of robotics won't be built in a lab. It will be built by people who care about what happens when technology meets the real world.

At TACTILIA, you'll work on one of the hardest open problems in robotics: giving machines the dexterity, reliability, and robustness they need to interact with the physical world at industrial scale.

The technology is taking shape. The team is being built. And the standards for robotic hands and their skills are still wide open.

That means your decisions will have a lasting impact — not just on a product, but on what comes next for Physical AI.

Build the hand. Define the standard. Shape what comes next.

If you're excited by the challenge of building robotic hands that work reliably in the real world, we'd love to hear from you.

Our Mission

Aleph Alpha is one of the few companies in Europe doing serious foundation model pre-training like our recently released Kolibri-1 model. Our customers - in finance, manufacturing, public administration - need models that understand German, meet European regulatory requirements, and work reliably in high-stakes settings. We're building that in Heidelberg.

Team Culture

At Aleph Alpha, we foster a culture built on ownership, autonomy, and empowerment. Teams and individual contributors are trusted to take responsibility for their work and drive meaningful impact. We maintain a flat organizational structure with efficient, supportive management that enables quick decision-making, open communication, and a strong sense of shared purpose.

We believe a strong engineering culture is the key to model training success. We like Extreme Programming and favor trunk-based development. We often mob-program, which keeps us aligned and means we always learn from each other.

About the Role

As an AI R&D Engineer in Model Training (f/m/d), you will join our model training team in Heidelberg or Berlin. Most of the team is based in Heidelberg. The model training team is building and improving our model training pipeline, which has been used to train Kolibri.

  • You will work across our full stack. Some weeks you might be optimizing how training loads are scheduled on our cluster and making the pipeline more robust and performant so we can iterate faster. Other weeks, you will be enabling large-scale code execution for reinforcement learning. And at other times, you might dig deep into our evaluation codebase to lift inference throughput on evals.

  • No two days are the same. Things move fast, and your ability to focus and prioritize is what lets you unblock the team day-to-day while designing the high-quality tooling and infrastructure that speeds us up long-term.

  • We're still building out our training pipeline and infrastructure. Some pieces exist, some do not, and you will have real influence on what gets built and how. Your work directly shapes how quickly we can experiment and improve our models.

  • Identifying issues and taking initiative is what drives our day-to-day work.

  • Working mode, design decisions, priorities are all done in your team together with your team mates.
    The strongest teams often use highly collaborative techniques, like mob or pair programming.

  • Due to the highly collaborative nature of our work you are expected to be on-site at least two days a week. If you are in Berlin, you should expect to travel around every second month for a few days to Heidelberg.

  • We are specifically looking to strengthen the Software Engineering in the teams which are research heavy. Major points include improving the maintainability of our code through tests and design & architecture changes.

Requirements

  • At its core, you need to be able to dive into a codebase, change the behavior as necessary, and after the change the code should be better tested and easier to understand than before.

  • As such we look for candidates for an understanding of how to design for low coupling and high cohesion paired with the ability to incrementally refactor.

  • Experience with the following technologies is likely to be helpful:

    • Test Driven Development (TDD)

    • Trunk based development

    • Continuous integration

    • Domain Driven Design

  • Most of our code is in Python, there is also the occasional Rust codebase.

We're looking for our first hospitality fan Sales person in NRW. Sales is at the heart of our business growth right now, and you will be driving it forward in your day-to-day. This role is about more than closing deals, it is about blending with the hospitality scene and winning the market.

What You’ll Do

Our sales are not your typical SaaS or office sales. We meet our customers where they operate:

  • Find the coolest new hospitality spots in town that everyone talks about

  • Create engaging ways to show our product

  • Do a smooth handover to the onboarding team to make sure we go live quickly and successfully

  • Efficiently use our CRM and other Sales tools (Hubspot, Clay, AI) to leave more time for creativity and connection

  • Keep an eye on the new developments in the industry and the merchants’ needs to create our own path

What You’ll Need

You are a natural relationship builder with a passion for hospitality industry:

  • Hands-on approach, independence and hunger for fast-paced operations

  • Natural curiosity and a healthy appetite for calculated risk - we want you to try new things and not be afraid to fail

  • Strong and engaging communication skills - you can grab an attention of a busy hospitality owner and keep them interested

  • Passion and curiosity for hospitality and hospitality tech

  • A minimum of 3 years of experience in Sales, Commercial Account Management or Hospitality

Benefits:

  • Competitive Salary & Uncapped Commission

  • Flexible time off

  • Team events

What is Restaurant Software?

Restaurants and other merchants use various software systems such as Point of Sale (POS), Reservations, Kitchen Display Systems (KDS), Payments, Inventory, Staffing, and the list goes on. These systems all need to speak to each other which they frequently don’t. It’s a mess, and we are fixing it.

From buying a croissant at a cafe to having dinner with friends, it’s a €4 Trillion+ global market and a critical part of everyday life in today's economy.

We use AI the way our merchants use Tebi, to cut out the friction and get to what matters faster. We believe in a world where AI increases quality, efficiency and speed.

At Tebi, AI isn't a policy or a checkbox, it's just part of how we work. It helps us write, analyse, build, and improve but doesn’t make the last call. If there's a smarter way to do something, we want to find it.

title: Part-time HR Generalist
description:
About 3E:

3E is a mission-driven company dedicated to creating a safer and more sustainable world. We offer award-winning regulatory intelligence and AI solutions to help organizations protect people and products. With over 35 years of experience and a global presence, we empower our customers with innovative compliance solutions. 

You will get to work at a company that combines startup agility with the stability of an industry leader. Partner with enterprise customers and global experts to advance environmental safety and solve complex data science challenges.

Join us and make an impact!

About the Role

3E is seeking a part-time HR Generalist with the ability to work remotely within Germany. In this position, you will use your HR expertise to support employees across Germany as part of our collaborative, international EMEA HR Operations team.

 

This permanent, part-time role is ideal for HR professionals with at least 3 years of HR experience. You will work approximately 3 days per week (20–24 hours weekly), partnering with HR colleagues to support all aspects of the employee lifecycle, from onboarding and HR administration to payroll coordination and HR operations. You’ll communicate in German, prepare German-language employment documentation, and ensure compliance with German employment requirements, all from a remote setting within Germany.

 

In addition to daily HR responsibilities, you will help advance operational excellence by researching German HR topics, maintaining Standard Operating Procedures, and developing HR team knowledge bases. You will also use AI-enabled tools such as Microsoft Copilot and ChatGPT to aid research, documentation, and productivity while ensuring confidentiality and sound judgment.

 

We are seeking an organized, proactive HR professional who enjoys collaborating virtually, thrives in a dynamic environment, and is eager to drive continuous improvement.

 

Location: Remote within Germany

 

What You'll Do

 

  • Coordinate onboarding and offboarding activities for employees in Germany.

  • Prepare German-language employment contracts, amendments, reference letters, confirmations, and employee communications.

  • Maintain accurate employee records and HR documentation in compliance with German employment regulations.

  • Respond to employee and manager HR inquiries in German and provide timely, customer-focused support.

  • Assist with HR case management, payroll coordination, benefits administration, and time and attendance activities.

  • Support compliance with German employment laws, statutory leave, insurance, and other HR administration processes.

  • Research HR topics and document processes to improve consistency, knowledge sharing, and operational efficiency.

  • Collaborate with HR Operations, Payroll, Finance, Legal, and external vendors to support an exceptional employee experience.

  • Support additional HR projects and continuous improvement initiatives as needed.

 

What Makes You a Great Fit

 

  • 3+ years of hands-on HR Generalist experience, ideally supporting the German market.

  • Native or near-native (C2) German language skills are required.

  • Professional working proficiency in English.

  • Strong organizational skills with exceptional attention to detail.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

  • Demonstrated initiative and ability to manage HR responsibilities independently.

  • Sound understanding of German labor law, employment practices, and HR administration.

  • Interest in payroll, benefits administration, and employee services.

description:
Camunda is the enterprise platform for agentic orchestration, enabling organizations to coordinate AI agents, people, and systems across complex, end-to-end business processes. Visionary in 2025 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Business Orchestration and Automation Technologies. ranked 3rd in Flexa's 2026 Most Flexible Companies, We’re growing fast and looking for top talent to join our team. If you want meaningful work, visible impact and put something genuinely rare on your CV, keep reading.

About the Role:

Hi there! We're hiring an Information Security Engineer with a focus on Application Security to join our Information Security team at Camunda.

We are a team that takes security seriously without making it feel like a locked door. We work in a transparent, straightforward way, and we care about doing the work right rather than just checking a compliance box.

You will work side by side with our R&D engineers: reviewing designs, threat modeling new features, digging into code and helping teams make good, risk-based decisions about the vulnerabilities that come in. You'll also help build the internal tools that make this work scale, including our CVE registry and the LLM-assisted workflows we use to analyse code and triage findings.

Camunda is an AI-first company, and InfoSec is no exception: AI agents are part of how we review code, assess vulnerabilities, and build our tools. You will help shape how that works.

This is a hands-on role for someone who already has solid AppSec foundations and wants to grow. We are a generalist team, so you will also take part in our on-call rotation and incident response, and get exposure to other areas of security. But most of your time will be spent with engineers and building and maintaining internal tools and processes.

What You Will Do

  • Vulnerability management: triage findings from SCA, container and code scanning, external reports and internal security testing; assess whether Camunda is actually affected; agree fix / mitigate / accept with engineering and follow through to release.

  • Threat modeling and security reviews: run threat modeling sessions and design reviews with R&D teams for new features and architecture changes, and turn the results into concrete, prioritised actions.

  • Code analysis with LLMs: use and improve LLM-assisted tooling (agents, prompts, reusable skills) to review code, validate findings and reproduce issues, while applying your own judgement to know when the model is wrong.

  • Build internal security tooling: contribute to the CVE registry and related automation that connects scanners, engineering teams, and customer communication. Much of it is built on Camunda itself.

  • Help engineers do the secure thing by default: answer questions, review pull requests, improve guidelines and occasionally run a session or workshop.

  • On-call and incident response: share the InfoSec on-call rotation with the other engineers and help investigate and resolve security incidents.

  • Support the wider team: help write security advisories for our customers, answer customer security questions and support audits.

What You Will Bring to the Role

  • Around 3+ years in security or software engineering, with at least 2 of them working on application or product security (AppSec, product security, pentesting, or a security-focused developer role all count).

  • Experience at a SaaS or software product company, working closely with engineering teams that ship often through modern CI/CD and cloud environments.

  • Hands-on vulnerability triage: you've worked with tools like Snyk, Trivy, Semgrep, CodeQL or similar, can tell a real issue from a false positive, and can explain how exploitable something actually is in context (CVSS, exploitability, configuration).

  • Threat modeling and design review experience (e.g. STRIDE) on real systems, ideally web apps, APIs, or distributed services.

  • You read and write code. You're comfortable reading Java (Camunda is built on it) well enough to follow a data flow and spot a security bug. You can write scripts and small tools and contribute to an existing codebase with review.

  • You build with AI, not just chat with it. You use AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot or similar) in your daily work to write tools, analyse code or automate tasks. And you know their output still needs a second look, especially when it comes to security.

  • Clear, friendly communication with engineers. You see yourself as an enabler, not a gatekeeper, and you can explain risk to people who aren't security specialists.

Nice to haves

  • Some Python and/or JavaScript experience, or experience building internal tools.

  • Willingness to learn and use Camunda, since we build a lot of our own security automation on it. Prior BPMN / workflow experience is a plus.

  • Experience responding to security incidents or being part of an on-call rotation.

  • Exposure to security advisories, CVE disclosure or bug bounty programmes.

  • Knowledge of AI/LLM security risks (OWASP Top 10 for LLMs / agentic apps, prompt injection, tool abuse).

  • Experience securing Kubernetes or container-based workloads, or open-source / B2B software.
