Doch unsere Arbeit endet nicht mit der Auslieferung. Wenn bei unseren Kunden technische Fragen auftreten, eine Anlage nicht wie erwartet funktioniert oder ein Serviceeinsatz erforderlich wird, braucht es jemanden, der zuhört, Zusammenhänge versteht und die richtige Lösung auf den Weg bringt.

Und genau hier kommst du ins Spiel.

Als technischer Serviceberater bist du eine wichtige Schnittstelle zwischen unseren Kunden und den technischen Bereichen bei Emission Partner. Du analysierst Probleme, begleitest Kundenanfragen bis zur Lösung und sorgst dafür, dass unsere Servicetechniker gut vorbereitet in ihre Einsätze starten können.

Du verstehst Technik, arbeitest gerne mit Menschen und hast Spaß daran, Problemen wirklich auf den Grund zu gehen? Dann werde Emission Partner.

Was du bei uns bewirkst



Du machst aus technischen Problemen konkrete Lösungen.

Wenn sich ein Kunde bei uns meldet, übernimmst du Verantwortung für sein Anliegen. Du versuchst zunächst zu verstehen, was technisch passiert, grenzt mögliche Fehlerursachen ein und entwickelst gemeinsam mit unseren Fachbereichen die passende Lösung.

Vieles lässt sich bereits aus dem Innendienst klären. Wird ein Einsatz vor Ort notwendig, sorgst du dafür, dass unsere Servicetechniker die relevanten Informationen haben und vorbereitet zum Kunden fahren können.

Und dein Wissen fließt zurück in unsere Produkte: Wiederkehrende Fehler und Erfahrungen aus dem Service helfen uns dabei, technische Lösungen weiterzuentwickeln und Probleme künftig möglichst schon im Vorfeld zu vermeiden.

Damit hilfst du nicht nur einem einzelnen Kunden, sondern machst unseren Service und unsere Produkte jeden Tag ein Stück besser.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Du unterstützt unsere Kunden bei der Fehlersuche und erarbeitest gemeinsam mit ihnen und unseren internen Fachbereichen geeignete Lösungen.
  • Du koordinierst technische Fragestellungen mit unseren Kollegen aus Service, Entwicklung, Elektrotechnik und weiteren Fachbereichen.
  • Du bereitest Serviceeinsätze vor und stellst den Technikern die notwendigen Informationen zu Fehlerbild, Anlage und Aufgabenstellung zur Verfügung.
  • Du dokumentierst Kundenanfragen, Fehlerbilder und gefundene Lösungen nachvollziehbar.

  • Du begleitest technische Anliegen so lange, bis für den Kunden eine tragfähige Lösung gefunden wurde.

Das bringst du mit



Uns ist wichtiger, dass du technische Zusammenhänge verstehst, lösungsorientiert denkst und gut mit Menschen umgehen kannst, als ein perfekter Lebenslauf.

  • Du hast idealerweise eine technische Berufsausbildung, beispielsweise im Bereich Elektronik, Elektrotechnik, Mechatronik oder einem vergleichbaren technischen Beruf.

Uns sind Gemeinschaft, Kreativität, Fairness, gegenseitiger Respekt und Spaß bei (und auch mal nach) der Arbeit wichtig.

  • In unserer Onboarding-Phase lernst du den SalesCoach, unsere Entwicklungsprozesse und unsere KI-Agenten kennen und begleitest ein laufendes Projekt, bevor du eigene übernimmst.

  • Du hast eine Leidenschaft für technologische Innovationen und die Motivation, kontinuierlich Neues zu lernen.

  • Passe deine Arbeitszeit fortlaufend an: 50 % / 60 % / 80 % / 100 %-Vertrag - ganz wie es zu der jeweiligen Lebenssituation passt.

title: Environment Artist
description:
About Techtive Games

Techtive Games is a Germany-based video game developer creating Ardem, an open-world survival game. Built by former modding veterans, the studio combines AA-level ambition with an independent mindset to push development practices forward and build immersive worlds built to be played, modified, and expanded.

We're looking for an Environment Artist to join our team as we move into full production on our debut game Ardem, an open world survival game developed in Unreal Engine 5.

In this role, your focus is asset production, with a strong emphasis on architecture and modularity. Our world artists build Ardem's world —> you create what they build it with: modular architecture kits, bespoke landmark structures, and the environmental assets that make the world feel believable and lived-in. You won't be doing level design yourself, but you need the instincts of someone who could — assets only work if they're made with world-building in mind. At Techtive, we believe in a creative workflow where everyone contributes to the final look and feel of the world. It's a team effort: you'll work closely with World Art, Tech Art, and 3D Art, using cutting-edge UE5 tech to push visuals to new heights.

One thing we care about a lot: we're hiring from our community. We want people who actually play survival games — not as market research, but because it's your genre. If you know from hundreds of hours in the genre why a base location feels right, why a ruin tells a story, or why clutter placement can make or break immersion, you already understand half the job. That's also why we'd love it if you share your Steam profile with your application — not as a gate, we're just genuinely curious where your gaming interests lie and how much they overlap with what we're building.

We value creativity, ownership, and personal growth. Rather than working through rigid ticket pipelines, our team members are encouraged to actively shape systems, improve workflows, and grow together not only on Ardem, but on future projects as well.

If you love building worlds players want to get lost in — and you've survived a few of them yourself — we'd love to hear from you.

Tasks

On a day to day basis, you will:

  • Create high-poly and low-poly models for environmental objects — with a clear focus on architecture: modular building kits, structures, and props

  • Overhaul and optimize our existing asset kits: consolidate materials, reduce poly counts, and bring everything to a consistent, performant standard

  • Create assets for bespoke landmark locations — the kind of places players remember

  • Design with modularity and reusability in mind, so our world artists can build more with less

  • Rework existing vegetation and natural assets to a cleaner, more maintainable standard where needed

  • Work from photo reference and concept art to hit a believable, grounded look

  • Produce clean, efficient UVs and game-ready assets that respect the technical limitations of a large open world

  • Work closely with World Art, Level Design, and Tech Art to ensure requirements are met

  • Help troubleshoot and fix problems as they arise, from a visual, technical, and production perspective

Requirements

  • Previous experience on professional game projects

  • A portfolio with clear examples of your own asset production — not just set dressing or kit-bashed scenes. On team pieces, tell us exactly which parts you made yourself; we do check.

  • Solid experience building modular asset kits, and a real understanding of how worlds are constructed from them

  • Strong modeling skills and experience in a major 3D package (Blender, Maya, 3ds Max)

  • Sculpting experience with software like ZBrush

  • Good understanding of the PBR material pipeline

  • Solid grasp of baking and texturing using the Substance Suite and Photoshop

  • Basic knowledge of shader creation

  • Ability to resolve issues from a visual, technical, and production perspective

  • Strong communication skills — you can articulate ideas and questions across departments, and give and receive constructive feedback

  • We’d appreciate a link to your Steam profile, so we can get a feel for where your interests lie and where they overlap with ours

  • Fluent spoken and written English

Bonus Skills

  • Proficiency with Unreal Engine 5

  • Knowledge of foliage creation

  • Experience with procedural workflows (e.g. Houdini)

  • Experience working on open world games

  • Experience working in an indie or small team environment

Working Model

  • Fully remote

  • Freelance, with a full time option for candidates based in Germany

  • Flexible working hours with a strong focus on ownership and trust

  • Direct collaboration within a small, focused team

Benefits

  • Work on Ardem, a highly anticipated survival game — and help set a new benchmark for the genre you love

  • Small team with high impact, results-driven mindset and fast decision-making

  • High ownership and creative freedom — shape the world, don't just fill tickets

  • Flexible working hours (results > green dots)

How We Hire

  1. First interview — We talk about Techtive, Ardem, and the role, and get a high-level picture of your skills and how you work.

  2. Art test — If the first conversation goes well, you'll receive a small art test: a basic brief with a few guidelines and some inspirational screenshots from Ardem. Everything you build should work as part of a larger environment — we're not looking for isolated beauty shots that would fall apart in an actual game world. There's no fixed deadline, but we'll ask you to track roughly where your time went.

  3. Second interview — We go through your art test together: your decisions, your process, and where you spent your time.

  4. Culture fit — The final conversation is less about craft and more about people: how you like to work, what you expect from a team, and whether we actually fit each other. We're a small, fully remote crew — who you are matters as much as what you build. The practical side (contract, conditions, start date) gets sorted here too.

We know an art test is a real time investment, and not everyone can afford that easily — we don't take it for granted. It's the fairest way we've found to judge actual craft over a polished portfolio, and it's the basis for a much better conversation in round two.

Deep Blue Recruitment is working with an international technology company looking to appoint an experienced Senior Privacy Counsel to join its legal team.

Operating in the enterprise technology sector, the business develops software and digital solutions for customers across a range of industries. With continued investment in emerging technologies, including AI, data protection is becoming an increasingly important consideration in how the business develops its products, manages risk and works with customers.

We're looking for a commercially minded privacy lawyer who enjoys working closely with the business, understanding how technology works and finding practical solutions to complex legal questions.

This is a broad, hands-on role combining privacy advisory work, commercial support and the continued development of internal data protection processes.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Advise colleagues across the business on a broad range of privacy and data protection matters, providing clear, commercially focused legal guidance.

  • Work closely with product, technology and commercial teams on the development of new services, ensuring privacy considerations are addressed early in the process.

  • Support the negotiation of commercial agreements, particularly around data processing, international transfers, customer relationships and third-party arrangements.

  • Advise on GDPR and other applicable international data protection regulations, helping the business understand and manage its obligations across different markets.

  • Provide legal guidance on emerging technologies, including AI, and the implications of new products and data processing activities from a privacy perspective.

  • Review and improve existing privacy policies, internal procedures and governance frameworks to ensure they remain practical and fit for purpose.

  • Work alongside information security and IT teams on data governance, risk assessments and privacy-related incidents.

  • Identify opportunities to improve the efficiency of privacy operations, including through automation and better internal processes.

  • Monitor regulatory developments affecting technology businesses, particularly around data protection, AI and digital services.

  • Provide training and guidance to colleagues across the organisation, helping non-legal teams understand their responsibilities when handling personal data.

What They're Looking For

  • A qualified lawyer with approximately 4-10 years of experience specialising in data protection, privacy or technology law, with significant experience advising B2B technology businesses, in an in-house setting.

  • Strong knowledge of GDPR and European data protection law, with proven experience applying these regulations in B2B software, SaaS, AI or technology infrastructure environments.

  • Hands-on experience advising companies that develop or provide enterprise software, AI platforms, cloud infrastructure, APIs or other data-intensive B2B technology solutions.

  • A good understanding of AI technologies, particularly AI models, infrastructure and enterprise applications, and the privacy and regulatory challenges associated with their development, deployment and commercialisation.

  • Experience advising on B2B commercial agreements, including data processing agreements (DPAs), international data transfers, enterprise customer contracts and complex controller/processor arrangements.

  • Comfortable working closely with product, engineering and infrastructure teams, understanding technical architectures, data flows and product development processes to provide practical, commercially focused legal advice.

  • A commercial approach to risk management, with an understanding of the challenges facing high-growth B2B technology companies and the ability to find workable solutions that support product development and commercial objectives.

  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple projects and competing priorities independently in a fast-moving technology environment.

  • Experience working within an international B2B technology business, particularly one scaling its enterprise customer base or operating across multiple jurisdictions, would be beneficial.

Why Consider This Opportunity?

This is an opportunity to join an international technology business where privacy plays an important role in how the company operates, develops its products and works with customers.

You'll have a broad remit, working closely with different teams across the organisation on a range of commercial, operational and regulatory matters, including some of the challenges emerging technologies bring to data protection.

If you're a privacy lawyer who enjoys working closely with the business, has an interest in technology and takes a practical approach to solving legal challenges, we'd be interested in hearing from you.

At hyperexponential, we’re building the AI-powered platform that enables the world’s most critical decisions in a $7 trillion industry - which risks to take, and how to price them. Until now, insurers have been making billion-dollar decisions using outdated tools. We’re changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.

Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we’re scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world’s largest insurers, with close to zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.

What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world’s first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn’t tied to title or tenure; it’s defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you’ll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.

If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.

About the Project Management team

The Project Management team takes hx customers from signed contract to live in production. We work in cross-functional pods alongside delivery engineers and solution architects, and we own the customer relationship day to day: the plan, the budget, the risks and the conversations that go with them. We work with some of the most sophisticated insurers in the world, including Lloyd’s syndicates, Tier 1 carriers, reinsurers and MGAs. We are moving to a shared, AI-first way of working, where one set of skills is used and improved by the whole team, and we are looking for people who want to help build it.

What you’ll be doing

  • Lead delivery across the projects in our Strategic pod, holding commercials to plan and surfacing risks early.

  • Lead and develop the people who report to you, so they progress.

  • Spot where a project can grow, and bring cross-sell and upsell opportunities to the account team.

  • Lead internal projects that change how the pod delivers, and feed them into our shared delivery framework.

  • Shape how AI is used in our delivery workflows, beyond your own work.

  • Work alongside the pod’s technical lead, so technical delivery can focus on technical problems.

What you’ll need to have done

  • Run several projects at once with commercial accountability.

  • Led people, through line management or equivalent, and be able to point to someone who progressed.

  • Changed how a team works and be able to show it was adopted.

  • Built or shaped AI-enabled workflows, and be able to explain what you learned.

You’re unlikely to thrive here if

  • You prefer to direct work from a distance, rather than stay close enough to the detail to make sound commercial and delivery calls.

  • You’re more comfortable following an established playbook than building one as the team and the product evolve.

  • You see leadership as managing tasks rather than developing people and holding them to a high standard.

If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you’ll do your best work. We’re building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.

Compensation

At hx, we’re committed to salary transparency. You’ll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we’re working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.

Because we’re building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don’t always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that’s competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.

title: Enterprise Account Executive
description:
A little about us

incident.io is the AI software reliability platform trusted by engineering teams at Notion, Linear, Ramp and 2,000+ companies who can't afford downtime.

The stakes are real, the talent is insane, and somehow it's a genuinely lovely place to work. We all pull our weight, go the extra mile, and put in the bit of magic most companies don't have time for, all while having fun and never taking ourselves too seriously.

We've raised $100+ million from Index Ventures, Insight Partners, and Point Nine, and we're growing fast. There's never been a better time to join.

The role in one line

As an Enterprise AE at incident, you sell to the engineering leaders who cannot afford to get incidents wrong, and every deal you close is one more company that handles its worst day better.

What that looks like day to day

As an Enterprise AE at incident, you're selling into the biggest and most complex accounts we go after, the ones where an incident going badly becomes a board-level problem. Intercom, Etsy, Miro, HashiCorp and StubHub are already customers, so you're not cold-starting a story nobody believes. The product has real market fit and it is nowhere near fully capitalised. That gap is the whole opportunity.

The team you're joining are seasoned sellers who are as much strategic partners and product evangelists as they are closers. Enterprise cycles here mean six or seven decision-makers, technical buyers who will test you properly, and C-level conversations where you need to be credible immediately. You'll run demos alongside SE's, and the feedback you bring back goes to a product team that ships in hours and days, not quarters.

Sales isn't a function bolted onto the side of this business, it's central to how we win. You'll work with leadership on building sales process rather than inheriting a finished one, and challenging how we do things is the job itself, not something you get credit for on top.

We're AI-forward, founded by engineers, and everyone here has unlimited Claude access. We expect you to use it properly: researching accounts, prepping deals, and moving faster than the rep across the table at a legacy vendor.

Who you are

  • You've closed $100k+ new business at the top end of enterprise, and you can talk me through how you actually did it, not just what the number was.

  • You're comfortable in a room full of engineers and CTOs. Technical buyers don't faze you, and you know the difference between selling to them and selling at them.

  • You're a proper hunter. You've got more than one way into an account, and a run of rejection doesn't take the wind out of you.

  • You build the case with evidence. Data, the right customer story, real product knowledge, whatever it takes to move that particular stakeholder.

  • Multi-threading is instinct, not technique. You assume there are six people on the other side of the deal and you'd rather know all of them.

  • You've got opinions about the product and you share them. The best reps here are the ones product actually listens to.

  • Startup ambiguity suits you. The playbook is half-written, nobody is going to hand you a process, and you'd rather help build one.

  • You're good to work with. You'll be close to leadership, SEs and CSMs, and you care about being someone people want in the room.

Supporting you

We work hard and we think life outside work matters just as much. Our benefits pack is built to support both.

  • Private medical insurance. Seriously good cover - we want you and the people you love to be looked after.

  • Competitive annual leave. Showing up at your best requires switching off, and we make sure you have time to do that.

  • First Friday of every month off. Yes, seriously.

  • Enhanced pension. We put real money in, because future-you deserves better than an afterthought.

  • Meaningful equity. We're rapidly scaling, and everyone who helps shape the outcome should share in it.

  • Unlimited AI spend. For everyone, not just engineers. We're all-in on AI across the company, and we expect you to be too.

  • Generous parental leave. The early days with a new baby matter more than anything we're doing here, and we want you to be present for them.

  • Two budgets that have your back. £1000 to invest in your setup, £500 a year to invest in yourself.

Compensation: £220K – £245K • Offers Equity

title: Senior Backend Engineer (Data serving)
description:

We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

Please note: applications will be open until Tuesday 13th October 2026 at 08.00 CEST.
We will not review any application before the closing date so please use this time to submit a high quality application.

About the role

We're looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to join the Data Serving team that owns the production-grade boundary between Pleo's raw product data and everyone who consumes it, including internal product teams, AI agents, and customers directly accessing their own data. This Senior Backend Engineer role builds and owns that boundary: APIs and the low-latency serving layer underneath it. You will build customer-facing infrastructure where contract stability and latency are non-negotiable, and where the clean abstraction you maintain is what lets every downstream consumer trust the data without ever touching a raw source.

Who you’ll be working with and reporting to

You will report to our VP of Data, and work closely with our Staff Data Platform Engineer, Data Engineers, Product Managers and others Engineers across the business. You'll also coordinate closely with the GenAI Platform and Data Infrastructure teams.

What you’ll be doing

As a Senior Backend Engineer, you will:

  • Build and own the Data API boundary: delivering clean, versioned, and performant endpoints for internal dashboards, customer-facing features, and third-party tools (e.g., Fivetran connectors via incremental syncs and cursor pagination).

  • Design and optimise the read models, indexes, and caching strategies in Postgres (and future OLAP stores) to guarantee low-latency query performance.

  • Build reliable integrations with Pleo’s Kotlin-based product backend services to ensure the serving layer surfaces the correct data required for a customer facing feature.

  • Own the reliability and performance of the services you build: monitoring, incident response, and SLOs appropriate to customer-facing infrastructure.

  • Partner with Data Engineers to define clean contracts between the ingestion/aggregation layer and the serving DB, ensuring read patterns match storage schemas.

  • Partner with the Authorization team to secure APIs using industry-standard authentication and authorization protocols.

  • Build a near-real-time data aggregation service to collect and unify data across Pleo services.

  • Design metadata, lineage, and governance capabilities that make the serving layer explainable, auditable, and trustworthy.

  • Own access control and permission management services, including row and column-level data access with full audit trails.

To put things into context, you can expect to work with the following tech stack: AWS (product side), GCP (data side), Docker, Kubernetes, BigQuery, PostgreSQL dbt, Kafka, Airflow, Python, Kotlin and more!

What you bring

You’ll thrive in this role if you have:

  • Strong backend engineering experience building and owning reporting and analytics API services and serving-layer infrastructure.

  • A mindset focusing on reliability, latency, and SLOs.

  • Experience owning API boundary layers including clean endpoint design, versioning, contract stability, and ensuring downstream consumers are never exposed to raw data sources.

  • Strong expertise designing performant read-heavy systems, including relational database optimisation, indexing strategies, materialised views, caching, and API performance tuning.

  • Solid database fundamentals (SQL and non-SQL) and strong SQL querying skills, as well as deep expertise in Kafka.

  • Deep experience with a JVM-based language (Pleo's product backend is Kotlin-based).

  • AWS or GCP with Kubernetes experience. You must be familiar with configuring, deploying and operating containerised applications in a k8s environment.

  • Experience working at the boundary between data systems and product backend services, with a real understanding of the operational differences between the two.

  • The ability to move quickly and independently. This is a hands-on delivery role with clear scope, not an architecture or advisory engagement.

  • Experience in fintech, payments, or other regulated product environments.

Why is this role a good fit for you

This role is a good fit for you if:

  • You are passionate about building systems that serve other engineers.

  • You understand what it means to design, build and maintain services with high performance, availability and reliability requirements.

  • You have a very deep understanding of the data world and know how to bridge the gap between data and engineering.

This role is not a good fit for you if:

  • You need to operate within very large and structured teams with clear hierarchy. This role sits within a small and specialist team with a lot of autonomy.

  • You do not wish to be responsible for services with high availability requirements. You will be held accountable for the quality and availability of those services alongside your team.

  • You prefer to be handed over clearly defined scope of work. You will be expected to define and design the solutions as much as building them.

How you’ll develop in this role

In your first 6 months at Pleo, you will:

  • Get deep into the current state: the upstream Kotlin services the serving layer will pull from, the internal consumers already waiting on the API (Data & AI Products, GenAI Platform), and any prototype serving logic that needs to be replaced or formalised.

  • Ship the first production version of the Reporting API (a defined set of endpoints with agreed contracts, versioning, and SLOs) with at least one internal consumer live against it.

  • Establish the access control, tenant isolation, and row/column-level security model for the API. You will have proven out low-latency query performance on Postgres, with clear metrics around reliability and SLOs, and established a clear architectural benchmark to understand when (or if) an OLAP layer would ever be necessary.

Please note: We can hire on a remote, hybrid or in-person set-up in any of the locations listed on the advert but you will need to be physically based in the country of your choice with a valid right to work. We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role in any of the listed locations.

Show me the benefits

  • Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)

  • Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office

  • Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis.

  • 25 days of annual leave + public holidays (additional days may apply in select countries based on local standards).

  • For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options.

  • We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far

  • Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work


The interview process

We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:

  1. Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background.

  2. Core skills test: An async AI-assisted programming test to assess your coding fundamentals.

  3. Hiring Manager interview: A 60-minute chat deep diving into your experience.

Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success!

With this in mind, we want to help you understand what we really care about when reviewing your application:

  • We receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI - it’s a big focus for us internally too- but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you - not AI - know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background.

  • Every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process.

  • This role focuses heavily on building services for internal / external users consumption. It is absolutely critical to have extensive API design and development experience, expertise in OLAP systems and to be able to work in Kotlin. Ensure your CV reflects clearly of the actual experience you have across those areas.

About your application

  • English first. Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us.

  • A fair look for everyone. Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails.

  • Interview at your best. We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email ----- We’ll design a process that works for you.

  • Your data is safe. When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes personal data, read our Privacy Policy here.

  • Applying for multiple roles? Nothing is stopping you, and we assess every role independently. However, we do look for alignment, so make sure you can explain why your interest and experience are right for each specific role.

  • Reapplying. If you’re applying for the same role again, please wait six months from your last decision before hitting submit.
